name: Hexagram of Dark Nourishment
xiang: Dark nourishment shows no image at all; its omens have not yet taken form. To stir invites disgrace and harm; withdraw and keep your virtue warm.
yan: When all twelve counters lie face down and show no characters, this is the Hexagram of Dark Nourishment. From the formed returning to the formless, the principle of Heaven and Earth, of yin and yang, is carried to its utmost. Thus the spirit counters begin with one and end in no image at all; the body having neither lines nor trigram, it falls outside the hundred and twenty-four hexagrams. In this hexagram nothing should yet be undertaken; in all things withdraw and preserve your hidden virtue, so as to dispel a great calamity. The sick will not die, but their recovery is slow and lingering. For the traveler it is inauspicious; it does not favor what is sought.
he: It is best to stay at home and keep to one's resolve; all affairs should be halted. In official matters, if you are guiltless you will be released, but if you are already implicated it will be hard to resolve. The battle line is unfavorable, and what you seek will not be gained.
chen: The Three Powers are not yet distinguished, and yin and yang are not yet discerned; this is the image of chaos before the primal division. No characters can be sought, and no meaning can be decided; hence the saying.
liu: The Supreme Ultimate is not yet divided, and all is dark and dim. Yin and yang are commingled, and no form can be discerned. Withdraw into stillness and silence so as to preserve your integrity. In this cast fortune and misfortune are not yet separated, and nothing may be undertaken; if you remain silent and guard yourself, it is auspicious and free of blame. Whoever draws it neither grieves at tidings of sorrow nor rejoices at tidings of joy; it is the hexagram of holding to constancy, of neither gain nor loss.
shi:
In days of many perils, tremble as you go;
be wary, as one treading upon thin ice, and know
the road ahead is fraught with peril and despair —
a lone lamp, unshaded, guttering in the air.

name: Hexagram of Transformation and Nurture
note: Lone yang, not yet bright; Qian, Heaven, northwest
xiang: Bright, bright is Heaven on high, shining down upon the earth below. It transforms and nurtures all that live, and opens wide the gates and doors. All affairs grow clear and open, and each beholds the other's face.
yan: When earth is matched with heaven, there is sure to be radiance and grace. It moistens the host of sprouts below, so that they grow and come to maturity.
he: In all matters follow your heart, and there will be little delay; this hexagram carries no blame. For a birth it is greatly auspicious and presages a son. Advancement in office is favored; in seeking wealth and hoped-for things there will be seals, credentials, and documents. For merchants meeting with nobles, all is fortunate. In official matters it is auspicious to make one's case through palace attendants, women, monks, or priests. The sick should not stay in a conspicuous place but remain within their room. The traveler's affairs are obstructed and he has not yet returned; but a campaign begun will surely win.
chen: One is the yang of heaven, and below is the configuration of earth. When yang qi emerges from the earth, the myriad things are transformed and born. As the verse says: 'Where the first yang begins to stir, before the myriad things are born.' Yin alone cannot give birth, and yang alone cannot send forth; therefore when yang qi is upon the earth, the earth's benefits are fair and abundant. Many hexagrams take their meaning from this.
liu: Heaven on high shines down and brings things to life. Each beholds the other, and none fails to flourish. In this cast yang comes to dwell in the position of earth; this is the image of Heaven's radiance shining down. In divining affairs, things begin to go well though not yet greatly; there is no blame.
shi:
You have reached a land of peace and calm,
with a thousand-mile road through river and hill.
Green willows and fragrant grasses line the way;
the wind is brisk, the horse's hooves are light.

name: Hexagram of Earth's Advantage
note: Yin dwelling in a yin position; Kun, Earth, southwest
xiang: When the root is set, affairs are settled, and men and things are all made right. Food and drink are clear and sweet, and each preserves his life and lot.
yan: Heaven is one and earth is two; hence the root. Once the root is established, men and things follow from it. Each attains his proper life and nature, and all affairs are mildly auspicious.
he: Once human affairs are settled, the essential thing is to set the foundation; each then preserves his life and nature, and all affairs are mildly auspicious. Seeking office or meeting with the noble are both favorable. The traveler will return only by autumn.
chen: Two is the body of pure and fair yin qi; dwelling in the lower position, it is the correctness of the way of earth. It bears the image of quiet and peace; hence the saying.
liu: With the root set and affairs settled, the way of earth is brought to completion. Food and drink are clear and sweet, and life and nature are preserved. In this cast, undertakings have both a beginning and an end; it is auspicious.
shi:
Apricots glow and plum blossoms breathe their sweet scent,
each burst of bloom bringing freshness anew.
If south of the river you meet one of the doubled mouth,
then change itself will rest with its master.

name: Hexagram of Founding Lords
note: Three yang aiding below; Qian, Heaven, northwest
xiang: Affairs rise and merit begins; here is the hero's founding ground. The sage and worthy redeem the world, and laws and ordinances are set in order.
yan: Three yang dwelling in the lower position is the image of rousing merit and establishing affairs. To create a foundation, none but a hero can bring it to completion. Therefore one is able to clarify the laws and redeem the world; all undertakings succeed, and governing people is likewise auspicious.
he: In all affairs there will be people to speak on your behalf and aid in your decisions. Planning affairs, advancing oneself, and seeking wealth are all auspicious. Official matters will be set in order. The traveler arrives, and with him come seals, credentials, and documents. The sick recover. A campaign is victorious. In all things, change and movement are favorable.
chen: Three is the fullness of yang; dwelling in the position of earth, it holds the image of a host of worthies founding a state — the flourishing of the way of earth. Hence the saying.
liu: Affairs rise and merit begins; the way of yang is established. The sage and worthy redeem the world, advancing to bring the enterprise to completion. In this cast three yang are in the position of earth, founding a base and building an enterprise; their firm vigor is sufficient for great action, and none can obstruct them. The diviner should greatly exert himself; all affairs are auspicious.
shi:
A single leaf of a boat has crossed the waves with ease,
and now at last it reaches the shore.
The cares of many years are only now fulfilled;
counting on my fingers, how many past griefs and hindrances!

name: Hexagram of Escorting the Departed
note: Pure yin holding sole sway; Kun, Earth, southwest
xiang: One nourishes the living and escorts the dead; the sacrifices are pure and abundant. The filial son leans upon his staff, and his garments are coarse and mourning-worn.
yan: This hexagram is the number of yin, the extreme of the myriad things. One receives his vital breath from heaven, is born as a person, and in death returns to the earth; hence 'nourish the living and escort the dead.' And when sacrifices are offered in due season, the filial son's service to his parents is brought to its end.
he: In this hexagram the filial son must practice utmost filiality, for there is fear of a death in the family; otherwise there will be mourning for a distant relative. For the sick it is inauspicious, and all affairs are unfavorable.
chen: Four is the extreme of yin; lying in the lower position, it holds the image of the dead entering the earth. Hence the saying. Yin at its extreme allows of no other undertaking.
liu: To nourish the living and escort the dead is the completion of the human way. The body and soul return to the earth and pass into oblivion. This cast is the image of extremity and exhaustion; whatever is divined is inauspicious.

name: Hexagram of Yang's Emergence
note: Lone yin without a master; Qian, Heaven, northwest
xiang: Heaven's light descends once more; the sun and moon shine forth their brightness. In all affairs and undertakings, whatever has feet may go its way.
yan: One yang springs forth, and therefore it is called Heaven's light. All that men and things are born with must depend upon the sun and moon. In this hexagram one should reckon for oneself and not trust to others.
he: One yang gives rise to the myriad things, and of itself finds the ground; yet above and below there is nothing solid, and one should not act lightly. In all affairs one must be sincere at heart, and it is auspicious to entrust matters to another. Seeking wealth brings much profit. Plans and undertakings succeed. Official affairs hold no suffering. The sick recover of themselves. The traveler returns only after a long while. An army marches to great victory.
chen: One returns as the yang of heaven and dwells in the position of man, as a person who receives the brightness of heaven and is given life thereby. Hence the saying.
liu: Heaven's light descends once more; the way of man is exalted. Whatever has feet may go, and no dark place is left unlit. In this cast a single yang stands at the center — the image of the sun and moon shining bright. It is that upon which men and things depend for life; in seeking affairs, one may hope, though only slowly.
shi:
You set out on a southern march in high spirits,
with blue sky and sun and moon shining bright.
The calamity is swept away and scattered;
fame is attained, and profit springs to life.

name: Hexagram of Reverence and Caution
note: Two yang rising from below; Qian, Heaven, northwest
xiang: Make virtue radiant and stop up what is wrong; in affairs, follow the turning of the moment. The worthy man is careful at the beginning; the noble man guards against the first faint sign.
yan: Although there is no superior position, the hexagram contains yang lines, sufficient to make one's abundant virtue radiant and to stop up wrong and transgression. It is also said: in all affairs one should act in accord with the moment, and must likewise guard against danger. For the noble man it is auspicious; for the petty man, inauspicious.
he: In all affairs, if one acts in accord with the moment, one attains one's aim. In the Zuo Tradition, Zang Aibo 'made virtue radiant and stopped up what was wrong' in presiding over the hundred officials; this hexagram is greatly auspicious for holding office.
chen: Both the way of man and the way of earth obtain one yang, yet it cannot yet flourish. However, with nothing above and no support below, one cannot but be cautious, wary, and self-guarding.
liu: To make virtue radiant and stop up wrong lies in following the season. To be careful at the end from the very beginning, one must guard against the faintest sign. In this cast one should discern the moment and know when to advance, and so carry out just and upright affairs.

name: Hexagram of the Sovereign Way
note: Yin and yang in communication; Gen, Mountain, northeast
xiang: Heaven and earth share one work; yin and yang communicate. The enterprise is vast and great, reaching from west to east. In its comings and goings, its traces are hard to follow.
yan: Heaven and earth open wide, and plants and trees are just beginning; one should not act loosely yet. It is best to accumulate virtue and cultivate benevolence, gradually turning toward flourishing. This is the image of a great lord, of a sage. What is plotted cannot yet be fathomed, what is sought is hard to obtain, and a far journey has not yet returned.
he: The ambition is great and hard to fulfill; it cannot be measured.
chen: The way of man is upright and the way of earth is upright; yin and yang attain each other, and this is the image of the realm set in peace and order. Hence the saying.
liu: Heaven and earth share one work; yin and yang attain each other. The enterprise is vast and great, and its advance has not yet reached its limit. Though one follows its traces, it cannot be fathomed. This cast is greatly auspicious for establishing merit and undertaking affairs.

name: Hexagram of Indecision
note: Many yang pressing and vying; Qian, Heaven, northwest
xiang: Foxy doubt and wavering; the mind is not resolved. To advance holds nothing to hope for; better to withdraw and follow what is right.
yan: In the superior position there is no ruler; the yang lines rise in contention — the image of things not yet settled. Within and without there is no response, hence the wavering. To act against reason is worse than to withdraw and hold to what is right.
he: Advance and retreat are undecided, and it is hard to follow one's heart; all affairs are like this. It is also said: office sought comes only late, but is auspicious. The sick recover only when their illness is grave. The traveler has not returned, and the battle line does not win. It is the image of withdrawing, reflecting, and following the ordinary course.
chen: The position of man is solitary and weak, while the position of earth is, on the contrary, flourishing; a host of bold ones rise together, yet none responds to another, and none knows whom to follow. Hence the saying.
liu: Foxy doubt and wavering, for there is none whom one can follow. To advance holds nothing to hope for, and the heart is full of restless longing. Better to withdraw and follow what is right, so as not to enter into peril. This cast falls at a time when there is no ruler's position, while the many yang are below and have no fixed direction; hence foxy doubt and wavering. There is yang without yin, and within and without there is no response; therefore advancing holds nothing to hope for, and it is better to withdraw and follow what is right. The diviner who keeps still will find fortune.

name: Hexagram of Flattery and Perversity
note: A host of yin overcoming yang; Gen, Mountain, northeast
xiang: Defying Heaven and turning against one's lord, heedless of all duty and order, they give rein to wicked flattery, and all men gnash their teeth at them.
yan: Above there is no position of Heaven, and in the middle one is solitary and weak; a host of yin usurps the mandate. Hence there are those who defy Heaven and flout reason — wicked flatterers who loathe the upright, maim the just, and bring harm upon good people. For holding office it is inauspicious; in a lawsuit, reason is lost.
he: People will surely denounce them, for by their own wantonness they bring it on themselves; hence 'gnash their teeth,' meaning their resentment runs deep. This hexagram is of secret plots contending with one another, of disaster in office and tangled trouble — greatly inauspicious. The sick should perform good deeds for merit. An army will not win. The traveler has not returned; it is best to cultivate virtue and follow the old ways.
chen: The way of man stands solitary while a host of the wicked rise together, secretly plotting to deceive those above; hence the saying.
liu: One lone yang amid a host of yin — the wicked veiling the upright. The petty man runs wanton, and none can restrain him. In this cast there is no position of Heaven above, and in the middle one is solitary and weak, while a host of yin consorts below and acts with unbridled will — the image of defying Heaven and turning against one's lord. Whatever is divined is inauspicious.

name: Hexagram of Yearly Abundance
note: Lone yin bereft of aid; Kun, Earth, southwest
xiang: Heaven and earth open wide; the myriad things all thrive. Affairs are just now decided; at year's end comes great abundance.
yan: This configuration is also like the hexagram of staying still; the work of Heaven and Earth in sowing and planting brings abundance in full measure. This hexagram is mildly auspicious. Plans proceed freely and smoothly, with no doubt or hindrance.
he: In all affairs good fortune comes slowly and should not be sought in haste. Hold yourself upright, and all matters will settle of themselves. What is lost or slipped away may yet be recovered.
chen: Two is the yin of earth, dwelling in the position of man, as one who receives the gentleness and yielding of earth in order to live, and enjoys the beauty of the earth's benefits. Hence the saying: two is able to unite with yang.
liu: The way of man is about to grow peaceful. In this cast, from one to two, the things that are born gradually multiply; undertakings gradually become possible.
shi:
Ever since I held my guard and stayed firm,
my merit stands before all the rest.
There is, besides, an extraordinary joy:
following the dragon up to the ninth heaven.

name: Hexagram of Caution Against Regret
note: Yin and yang misplaced; Zhen, Thunder, due east
xiang: Above and below are turned upside down; in all affairs the fit is lost. East and west go counter to each other, and none can follow in another's steps.
yan: There is sure to be some going forth, but affairs do not follow the heart, because yin and yang are misplaced. What is sought brings no benefit, and undertakings do not go smoothly.
he: Yin dwells in the central position, and inner yin presides over affairs. What is planned should favor yin, with people acting in harmony and accord. It is also said: office sought is not obtained, wealth sought is mostly lost, the noble is hard to see, official matters do not come out, the sick have not recovered, the traveler has not arrived, marriage is not yet joined, and an army does not win. It is best to follow the old course, or to go a thousand li away; that is auspicious.
chen: Yin, on the contrary, dwells above, and yang, on the contrary, dwells below — topsy-turvy and disordered. Hence the saying.
liu: Above and below are turned upside down; the yielding is exalted above the firm. East and west go counter to each other, and hopes are disappointed. In this cast there is no position of Heaven above, while yin and yang below are inverted; all things are turned contrary and rebellious — inauspicious. The diviner should guard himself with care.
shi:
The affairs of Heaven are turning toward peril,
and the human heart deceives even itself.
Watch men's words and guard against wrongdoing;
whether you advance or retreat, be careful in all you do.

name: Hexagram of Heeding the Beginning
note: Pure yin lacking yang; Kun, Earth, southwest
xiang: Think deeply and consider far ahead; dwell in the solid and ponder the peril. Though now there is no harm, in the end there will be ruin and loss. Walk ever in the upright way; be careful never to deceive.
yan: Pure yin without yang cannot secure good fortune to the end, and so ruin and failure are sure to appear. In this hexagram, though at first one enjoys a stolen ease, afterward blame is sure to appear.
he: In all affairs one should think deeply and consider far; though all is now peaceful and good, in the end it will be unfavorable. It is also said: be careful in both public and private matters; in official affairs there is someone of influence to be sought. The sick will not fall into utter ruin. The traveler has not returned. All else is unfavorable.
chen: Above and below are purely yielding, and have not yet reached the extreme; hence the saying.
liu: To think deeply and consider far is to dwell at ease in softness and timidity. In the end there is sure to be ruin and loss, for above there is no master. If one ever walks the upright way, one will not lose one's place. In this cast two yin twine together below while above there is no master; one may enjoy a stolen ease for the moment, but in the end cannot stand on one's own. The diviner who holds to the right can preserve himself; if he acts rashly, he is sure to come to ruin.

name: Hexagram of Blessings Converging
note: Three yang aiding yin; Zhen, Thunder, due east
xiang: Virtue dispels what is inauspicious; reverence and care should be observed. Though now obscure and hidden, blessings and emolument will come of themselves.
yan: This hexagram changes its yin and becomes a yang position, sufficient to exorcise the inauspicious and in the end bring blessings and emolument. In all affairs there is first a small worry, then great good fortune.
he: Blessings and emolument are sure to come, only not swiftly; affairs follow the heart. It is also said: public affairs at first make a stir, but afterward there is no contention. An illness at first is light, then grows grave; performing rites of exorcism is auspicious. For the traveler, the army, and commercial ventures, the beginning is unfavorable.
chen: Though the way of man is yin, the way of earth is flourishing with yang — a confluence of blessings. Hence 'blessings converge; be reverent and careful.' In general, the soft and yielding person cannot hold firm, and so there are many warnings of caution.
liu: Virtue dispels the inauspicious — yang beneath yang. Blessings and emolument come of themselves, and in the end one gains one's heart's desire. In this cast, though yin and yang are out of place, the three yang are firm and flourishing, and yin cannot overcome them; hence the image of virtue dispelling the inauspicious. At first there may be difficulty, but in the end great fortune is obtained; the tendency is natural and need not be sought. All things divined are auspicious.
shi:
The eagle grows more valiant as autumn comes;
riding the wind, it beats its wings to the Moon Palace.
If you ask when glory and splendor will arrive —
your renown will reach the ninefold heights, before and after.

name: Hexagram of the Hidden Traitor
note: Yin flourishing, yang lost; Kun, Earth, southwest
xiang: The hidden traitor plots rebellion; it bodes no good for later times. Though for now all suits your will, afterward too there will be no peace.
yan: Yang changed and yin obtained — this is the image of the hidden traitor. The hidden traitor plots harm, and one's heirs will grow feeble; hence 'it bodes no good for later times.' In this hexagram, in all affairs and undertakings, one first gains good fortune and afterward suffers harm.
he: A host of yin is at work, and so there are many hidden traitors, secretly plotting to harm others. Whatever is plotted does not succeed; even if it goes as you wish, in the end it is not auspicious. It is also said: yang changing into yin is the omen of petty men plotting against their superiors.
chen: The way of man is bright, and yet the following crowd is numerous; their rebellious plots are dark and secret. Hence the saying.
liu: The hidden traitor plots rebellion — the petty man has his hour. Of this cast Yan Youming says: yang changed and yin obtained is the image of the hidden traitor; in planning affairs, at first good fortune, then misfortune.
shi:
A single flower was about to bloom,
but met with wind and rain.
The clouds part, dark and blue-black;
all blessings and emolument vanish into emptiness.

name: Hexagram of Human Affairs
note: Flourishing yang at the center; Qian, Heaven, northwest
xiang: Human affairs are just arising; all is auspicious, nothing unfavorable. Those at home gain blessings; the traveler is sure to arrive.
yan: Three yang dwell at the center, and the way of man begins to flourish. Though there is no response or aid, in the end great good fortune is attained.
he: In all affairs, whatever is sought goes through and succeeds. The traveler is sure to arrive, and returns on schedule. Seeking office, meeting the noble, and planning affairs all succeed. The patient's illness is sure to retreat at the change of the season.
chen: Three is the fullness of yang, dwelling in the central position — the flourishing of the way of man. Man is born in the yin hour, the time when three yang come together in peace; hence the saying.
liu: Human affairs are just arising, and yang is at the true center; all is auspicious, nothing unfavorable, with a great and complete end. In this cast three yang emerge from the earth — the month of the yin hour, the season when human affairs just arise, when Heaven and Earth come together in peace. All is auspicious, nothing unfavorable.

name: Hexagram of Blessings and Profit
note: Two yang presiding over affairs; Qian, Heaven, northwest
xiang: Going out, you meet with blessing, and come together with the good. A bright pearl shines in the night, keeping me from all confusion.
yan: The virtue of yang is just now pervading, and it meets with blessing besides; all affairs are auspicious, and whatever is done goes through.
he: It meets with blessing, and is a bright pearl besides; whatever it shines upon is without exception auspicious, whatever is done succeeds, and lawsuits bring no harm.
chen: The way of man is firm and upright, and the way of earth is solid; blessings and emolument are both cultivated. Hence the saying.
liu: Going out, you meet with blessing — you gain your companions. A bright pearl shines in the night; even in the dark one is not blind. In this cast yang finds its kind and does not lose its order; the firm brightness of three is enough to illuminate the darkest places. Truly this is one who comes together with the good. Whatever is divined is auspicious.
shi:
Fortune arrives, and fame and merit come;
the sovereign's grace suddenly reaches home.
The peach and plum trees of many years
burst into bloom and fill the whole garden in spring.

name: Hexagram of Blessings and Good Fortune
note: Yin and yang each at rest; Gen, Mountain, northeast
xiang: Heaven rests and earth grows still; the worthy man is settled in his office. Going out or staying in, all is prospering and fortunate; the benefit is without limit.
yan: Heaven rests and earth grows still, yin and yang each at peace in its own place; the noble man is quiet and content in himself. In this hexagram all affairs return to their root; it is greatly auspicious and profitable.
he: What is sought cannot be gained quickly, yet the ten thousand affairs all follow the heart. Seeking wealth and hoped-for things are both auspicious. In lawsuits there is someone of influence to rescue you. The sick obtain a good physician. A campaign wins. It is an omen of great good fortune.
chen: The way of man is strong and flourishing, and the way of earth is pure and fair; yin and yang attain each other. Hence the saying.
liu: The worthy man is settled in office; his position is true and proper. Going out or staying in, all is prospering and fortunate, and he is content with nothing to fear. Of this cast Yan Youming says: yin and yang each at peace in its place, the noble man quiet and content in himself, all affairs returning to their root — greatly auspicious. He Chengtian says: what is sought cannot be gained quickly, and so the ten thousand affairs follow the heart — auspicious.

name: Hexagram of Right Ordering
note: Two yang of pure firmness; Qian, Heaven, northwest
xiang: A phoenix, bearing a pearl in its beak, comes to settle in a corner of the court. Blessing is brought to me, and calamity is taken away.
yan: Living in an age of flourishing position, one alone is able to govern it with pure firmness — an omen of good fortune; calamity dissolves and blessing arrives. The phoenix is the fairest of the five numinous creatures; the pearl is a treasure and plaything. What is sought is greatly auspicious, with no punishment or harm at all.
he: Blessings and emolument are just now arriving — greatly auspicious and profitable. It is an omen that wealth and goods will be doubled in measure.
chen: Above and below are abundant yang, with no yin to overcome them; a hundred blessings come of themselves. Hence the saying.
liu: The phoenix settles in the court — worthy virtue shines. Blessing arrives and calamity is removed; a host of good things return. Of this cast Yan Youming says: at a time when the position of Heaven is not yet settled, to be able to govern it with pure firmness is an image of great fortune. The diviner finds nothing unfavorable; only in praying for rain will he go against what he wishes.
shi:
Auspicious things and celebrations arrive together,
radiance and splendor fresh in five colors.
Heaven's grace has come today;
blessing and emolument rest upon this person.

name: Hexagram of Decline Overturned
note: Three yang concealing their brightness; Gen, Mountain, northeast
xiang: The noble man holds his ground; the petty man bows low his body. A wise lord governs the age, distinguishing purple from vermilion.
yan: Dwelling in the security of an important position, one receives the illumination of three yang. The Book of Changes says: it is a time when the petty man is not employed. Seeking office is greatly auspicious, and all other affairs attain their proper order.
he: With a wise lord above, the noble man obtains employment, and his wishes follow his heart; the petty man bows low and submits, as is only proper.
chen: Abundant yang is above and abundant yin is below; yin and yang respond to each other, and noble man and petty man each attain his proper portion. Hence the saying.
liu: The noble man gains his position, and the petty man submits. Purple is distinguished from vermilion, and each is settled in his office. In this cast yin and yang are each at peace in their places; firm brightness shines from above, while gentle yin follows below. Affairs divined attain their proper order; both noble man and petty man are fortunate.
shi:
Spring draws near to the withered tree;
the mountains and rivers brim with fair qi.
Two magpies chatter before the door —
joyful tidings that fame and profit are accomplished.

name: Hexagram of Preserving the Self
note: Accumulated yin at the center; Kun, Earth, southwest
xiang: The ghostly qi has not yet grown strong; the baleful poison has not yet taken form. Guard well your life and nature, and your household will be at peace.
yan: The central position is the image of man, and so it is said the ghostly qi is not yet strong. Yet dwelling in weak yin with no connection, one should carefully preserve the self and withdraw into seclusion, walking upright and cultivating virtue, so as not to be invaded by ghosts and baleful forces. To act is sure to fail and cannot be auspicious. Be warned.
he: It is best to preserve the self in quiet and stillness; on the whole it is not auspicious. The ghostly qi is rather heavy, and it is not fitting to divine about illness. In official affairs there is slander and harm at first, but later one is cleared and freed. The traveler arrives. The army wins.
chen: Four is the extreme of yin, dwelling in the position of man; if not death in old age, there is sure to be ghostly balefulness. One should only preserve oneself; hence the saying.
liu: The ghostly balefulness is not yet strong, and it is drawn into fellowship. To preserve and guard one's nature, one should dwell at peace. Of this cast Yan Youming says: the central position is the image of man, and so it is said the ghostly qi is not yet strong — because yin dwells in a yang position and is something to rely upon. If the diviner is careful, withdraws into seclusion, and preserves the self, there is no blame.
shi:
A flower met by spring rain can hardly keep its brightness;
water flowing east — how can its waves return?
If you set out on the road toward fame and profit,
beware of idle affairs and hidden worries in abundance.

name: Hexagram of the Unmanifest
note: Lone yang rising over yin; Zhen, Thunder, due east
xiang: The hidden dragon is about to rise; dark clouds mount up above. The world below is bathed in blessing; first adversity, then joy.
yan: Though at first it is not good, afterward comes great joy. One yang is below; in the Book of Changes, at the first line of nine, 'the hidden dragon is not yet to be employed.' As the dragon is about to rise and the clouds mount up to follow it, they fly together through the void and govern the world below — the omen of lord and minister attaining each other.
he: First adversity, then peace; all affairs are auspicious.
chen: Abundant yin is above and one yang below, cherishing the will to rise and advance; there is the image of cloud and dragon, one above the other. Hence the saying — it speaks of what is not yet manifest in the world.
liu: The hidden dragon gains its clouds and ascends to heaven. First adversity, then joy; in going forward, nothing stands before it. In this cast there is no Heaven above, while one yang is below and four yin receive it; hence the image of the hidden dragon gaining its clouds. Though at first there is hardship, afterward one succeeds — an omen of great fortune.
shi:
The waning moon grows full again;
the flowering branch is more vivid than before.
On the road back to the Peach Blossom Spring,
one day you meet an immortal.

name: Hexagram of Swaying Recurrence
note: Pure yin without response; Kun, Earth, southwest
xiang: The heavenly dragon rages; the Thunder Lord beats his drum. Clouds rise and rain is sent, and floods pour down upon the earth.
yan: With pure yin dwelling in a place without response, one cannot dispel calamity or ward off misfortune; hence it is said: thunder and lightning strike across, and floods become a disaster. In this hexagram all affairs are regrettable; for the traveler, for marriage, and for trade, all is unfavorable.
he: Rain pours and washes everything away; all affairs are regrettable. It is an unfit hexagram.
chen: Below there are two yin, rising to become the center; four yin shroud the utmost. It is the image of drifting and tossing, of turning back and forth. Hence the saying.
liu: The heavenly dragon rages — yin rises above. Floods pour down upon the earth, and nothing can withstand them. Of this cast Yan Youming says: with pure yin dwelling in a place without response, one cannot dispel calamity or ward off misfortune, and so disaster and blame are incurred. Whatever is divined is inauspicious; it is fitting only for praying for rain.
shi:
Pouring and sipping the wine in the cup,
lingering among the flowers beyond the rail —
in the midst of a joyful banquet,
I do not notice the sun already slanting west.

name: Hexagram of Retreating from the World
note: Yin overmastering yang; Zhen, Thunder, due east
xiang: The petty man attains his aim; the noble man loses his way. He leaves his house and hall, and enters the marshland grasses.
yan: With the virtue of bright yang, one withdraws to a lowly place, while the dark and shady sort, on the contrary, hold the central position — the image of the worthy and good being thwarted and detained. Therefore one abandons his hall and beams and takes distant shelter among the marshes and reeds, dwelling in seclusion, nurturing his will, and awaiting his season. This hexagram favors retreat, not advance.
he: Overmastered by yin, one has lost his proper place. It is also said: the sick should make it known, and a woman will save and cure them. The traveler is on the road. All affairs are mediocre.
chen: A host of yin is above, and the petty man attains his aim. The three yang are of complete talent, yet on the contrary they dwell below — the image of the noble man in the wilds. This hexagram differs from the one of four in the middle and one below: there one yang could still advance, but here three yang have reached their limit and cannot advance; hence the image is taken differently, and so the saying.
liu: The petty man attains his aim — yin rides over yang. Entering the marshland grasses, one's position is not fitting. In this cast yin and yang are out of place; in all affairs, to retreat is auspicious and to advance is inauspicious.
shi:
Quarrels and slander come to your very door,
and disaster lingers within your person.
Before men, beware the hidden arrow;
above all, fear the loss of your wealth.

name: Hexagram of Stirring Ghosts
image: Image of Employing the Occult Arts
note: Two yin contending and struggling; Kun, Earth, southwest
xiang: Two ghosts dwell together, ever suffering hunger and want. They would enter my door, but fear this sacred talisman.
yan: At a time of accumulated yin, ghosts are about to do harm; with no master for the sacrifices, hence it is said they suffer hunger and want. The ghosts do not dare approach people, for they still fear the sacred talisman. In this hexagram one should write talismans and chant spells to expel ghostly evil; by offering sacrifice one gains good fortune.
he: Blessing departs and calamity comes; one should cultivate merit and virtue, and do good to expel evil. For the sick, only by writing talismans and chanting spells will they be cured. The fields and silkworms yield a scanty harvest. Nothing goes as one wishes; it is an ordinary, undistinguished hexagram. The earth gods and ancestors are unsettled, affairs are many, ghostly theft and illness are frequent, and there is agitation, oppression, fright, and worry; going out to avoid them is auspicious.
chen: The two positions are yin at its extreme, and cannot accomplish anything; like a crowd pressing from above and below, they should be dealt with by proper methods. Hence the saying. This differs from the one of two in the middle and two below: lesser yin is pure and fair, while old yin is at its extreme and of no use.
liu: Two ghosts dwell together — accumulated yin hides itself. They fear this sacred talisman; in their extremity they have nowhere to go. In this cast two yin dwell below with no position above, and there is no master of the ancestral shrine and sacrifices; these are what are called ghosts without support. Though the position of Heaven is void, the high and bright dwell above, and the ghosts cannot go up; there is still the sacred talisman to restrain them, so they cannot enter the door. Affairs divined are greatly troubled. For the sick, one should write talismans and chant spells to cure them.

name: Hexagram of the Not-Yet-Bright
note: Lone yang bereft of aid; Qian, Heaven, northwest
xiang: The primal qi is newly born; the myriad things have not yet taken form. Its brightness is not yet fused, and going out and coming in are dark. Though one would begin to move and stand, of a hundred affairs none succeeds.
yan: One is the beginning of the myriad things. Yang qi is newly born and cannot yet be bright. It begins from a single line, seeking after the many images. In all affairs there is delay and lingering; one cannot yet fulfill one's wishes. It is best to await the season and then move.
he: Undertakings do not succeed. The sick gradually recover. All matters are mediocre. What is sought is not yet gained. Advancement in office and seeking wealth are both unfulfilled. Sending out troops and making arrests should both be avoided. The traveler is detained and will return only after the new year begins.
chen: The primal qi is first divided, and faint yang begins to be born; obtaining the One, it grows clear, but the turbid yin is not yet settled. Hence the saying.
liu: The primal qi is newly born, and has not yet found its companions. Going out and coming in are dark, and the hidden cannot be seen. In this cast, undertakings do not succeed, and all matters are mediocre.
shi:
To lean on the heart and gaze in hope is no good plan;
half seems real, and half seems nothing.
What you long for is not achieved, and what you do not hope for is gained;
with intent you end like one who climbs a tree to catch a fish.
One timber cannot bear the weight; one man cannot raise the work.
The courage of a single general can hardly quell the sudden fray.
To found a beginning and achieve a merit, only a multitude can bring it to completion.

name: Hexagram of Slight Loss
note: Two yang standing apart; Qian, Heaven, northwest
xiang: Climbing a tree to gather mulberry leaves, you fall to the ground and lie prostrate. The eastern neighbor has a remedy; you hasten there to ask the prescription. And so you meet a good physician, and escape without injury.
yan: Yin has lost its place and the yang line has no response, like the image of climbing high and falling to the ground. By seeking the prescription from the eastern neighbor, one escapes injury. For the east is the beginning of yang; the sick should go east to give thanks. In seeking wealth, in trade, in moving, and in recovering what is lost, one should seek to the east; then affairs will be auspicious. The traveler has not returned. Official matters are hard to resolve.
he: Having gone somewhere to fetch a thing, you fall ill because of it; if you return to the former place and give thanks, you will revive.
chen: Above and below are solitary, and the central position is void; he who is above bears the image of toppling and falling. Yet if he descends he may find safety, for the way of earth is secure when it has yang qi. Hence the saying.
liu: Climbing a tree and falling to the ground — to climb high is to be in danger. Asking the prescription and obtaining the medicine, one suffers no loss in the end. Of this cast Yan Youming says: yin has lost its place and yang has no response — the image of climbing high and falling to the ground; yet above and below are both yang with no yin, and so the disaster is not severe. The east is the beginning of yang; hence one asks the prescription of the eastern neighbor and obtains a physician. The sick fell ill because of something they fetched; if they return to the former place and give thanks, it is auspicious.

name: Hexagram of Partial Accord
note: Yin and yang in their proper places; Gen, Mountain, northeast
xiang: Like a newly taken bride, not yet in harmony within the home, strive earnestly by your own strength, and the family line will then continue.
yan: Two yin and one yang, their ways intersect and flourish; though there is no central line, yin and yang attain each other, and within and without respond — like entering a new marriage, which only afterward becomes harmonious. In all affairs there is response, and one can rely on oneself, vigilant by day and wary by night; even in danger there is no blame. The sick and official affairs hold no suffering; all affairs are auspicious.
he: Marriage has no beginning but has an end. Trade is profitable. Official matters are hard to accomplish. This hexagram is auspicious in all affairs.
chen: Yin and yang fundamentally respond to each other, but the center is void, and so there is a barrier in feeling and they are not joined at first; with time all is settled. Hence the saying.
liu: The bride is not yet familiar, and their feelings are not yet in accord. Striving earnestly by one's own strength, one builds the household. In this cast yang is above and yin below, each in its proper place yet not intimate, like a newly taken bride — their feelings, though in communication, are not yet fully harmonious. However, the central position is unobstructed, and though distant, they are near in the end; hence, striving earnestly by one's own strength, one is at last able to be in harmony. In divining affairs, if they are to your liking, you must still exert yourself. A campaign ends in reconciliation.
shi:
What household's maiden takes up spear and lance?
Know that profit and emolument are to be sought from her.
When at last it reaches its full course, all ends in joy;
do not refuse delight and love — for now, wander at ease.

name: Hexagram of the Unplowed
note: Two yang standing apart; Qian, Heaven, northwest
xiang: The soil is hard and the stones are firm; one lifts his head and appeals to heaven. The plowshare is not raised, and the standing grain is lacking.
yan: Within and without are both yang, and in the middle there is no human qi; the moisture does not flow through. Plowing and weeding are both abandoned, and so one lifts his head and appeals to heaven, hoping for rain.
he: In all affairs one must seek them, and then they succeed; if one does not seek, there is no achievement. Without plowing there is hunger; without rain there is drought. All affairs are as usual, and fields and silkworms likewise. In official matters one is wronged and suppressed, and the call for help is not yet answered. The grave illness can still be treated. The traveler is abroad.
chen: The way of earth is yang at its extreme, and above there is no yin to respond — like an unplowed field, or like the land in time of drought. Hence the saying.
liu: The soil is hard and the stones are firm — firmness without harmony. Lifting his head and appealing to heaven, there is nothing he can do. In this cast two yang dwell in the position of earth without response, and one yang is above while the central position is empty; cut off from one another, they cannot bring forth life. All affairs divined are empty — toil without achievement.

name: Hexagram of Ghostly Calamity
note: Yin and yang separated; Gen, Mountain, northeast
xiang: Within the house are baleful ghosts, two seated facing one another, lying in wait for faults and failings, cutting off water and fire. The gods of heaven and earth keep strict watch upon the faults of men.
yan: Yin and yang are at violent odds and do not restrain each other; the position of man is also vacant, with none to act as master of the house, and so baleful ghosts multiply in truth. In this hexagram all affairs are inauspicious; divining about the dwelling or the sick is calamitous.
he: In all affairs be careful; every movement brings disaster. One should cultivate blessings and avert calamity, and be wary of water and fire. Official affairs are inauspicious. The traveler has not returned.
chen: The central position has no person, and a host of yin is below — the image of ghostly qi brimming over; the one yang cannot restrain them. Hence the saying.
liu: Within the house are baleful ghosts — accumulated yin qi. The high yang stands alone and cut off, with no central position. Water and fire are cut off, and people are brought to ruin. Of this cast Yan Youming says: yin and yang are at violent odds and do not restrain each other; the position of man is also vacant, with none to act as master of the house, and so baleful ghosts multiply in truth. All affairs are inauspicious; divining about the dwelling or the sick is especially calamitous.
shi:
The empty house has long lain buried in dust;
every move brings trouble and delay.
It is only because one's fate is hard
that hidden misfortune twines itself about the body.

name: Hexagram of Bitter Restraint
note: Two yang standing in isolation; Qian, Heaven, northwest
xiang: Living in poverty and hardship, with no gate or door at all, going out and coming in among the tallow trees, without even a patch of earth to stand an awl.
yan: Far apart and set off from the rest, one dwells alone in his position; without there is no response, and within there is nowhere to dwell. Poverty, bitterness, and hardship — nothing but the tallow trees. This hexagram is unfavorable in all affairs.
he: Dwelling without support, hence it is said 'without even a patch of earth to stand an awl.' The sick sink into deep distress. What is sought is not attained. Official matters are hard to resolve. On a far journey one meets with robbers. In all things one should pray for blessings.
chen: Lone yang without response, and the way of earth empty and void — the image of poverty and bitterness. Hence the saying.
liu: Living in poverty and hardship, there is nothing with which to make a home. Going out and coming in among the tallow trees — how lamentable. In this cast the upper and middle are solitary, and there is no lower position; hence the image of poverty and cold without land. All affairs divined are inauspicious.

name: Hexagram of Great Openness
xiang: From small to great, there is no stumbling or wandering; from below ascending high, one reaches wealth and eminence. It is fitting to go on a far journey; it does not favor lying low in concealment.
yan: Aspiring from the small to the great, one can attain wealth and eminence; but if one dwells in the great and longs for the small, there is danger and ruin. It is also said: once Heaven and Earth are set in place, the sage joins with them, ordering the world in its raw obscurity, opening the origin and making the beginning. Hence 'from below ascending high.' In establishing merit and creating institutions, there is nothing that is not good. One should not plot in secret or scheme in the dark. It is not fitting for the old or the sick. Marriage is hard to join, because of the pure yang. The traveler divined has not returned. The imprisoned will be released. Trade is profitable.
he: The scholar and official rise high in office; it is fitting to be conspicuous, not concealed. The sick should not dwell in dark places but should go outside to avoid them — auspicious. There is no quarrel or slander; staying at home, keep to constancy. A campaign is auspicious, and battle is won. The pregnant will bear a son. Fields, silkworms, fishing, and hunting bring great gains — auspicious and profitable.
chen: The beginning of the one qi, the starting point of the Three Powers — pure yang of utmost vigor, advancing and advancing without cease. It joins in body with Qian, and hence the saying — this is primal success.
liu: From small to great, yang is just beginning to be born. Three men of one mind — it is fitting to roam abroad. It does not favor lying low, for its way is bright and clear. In this cast all three positions are yang, and the lesser yang is just now growing; hence the image of going from small to great, of ascending from below to the heights. The diviner who obtains it, in founding affairs and building an enterprise, in seeking fame and profit, finds all auspicious. In a lawsuit one should seek justice by open and fair means. The traveler is fortunate but has not yet returned. One should not engage in secret plotting or hidden and furtive affairs; the sick should go outside to avoid them — auspicious.
shi:
Like a leopard changing to patterned color,
riding the dragon, blessing comes of itself.
With bare body you receive wealth and honor;
in every affair there can be renewal.

name: Hexagram of Gradual Peace
note: Yin upright in its place; Xun, Wind, southeast
xiang: Dwelling at peace, one sets out his enterprise; there are people to manage the estate. He is both rich and honored, though the emolument and rank are not yet reached.
yan: If one calms the mind and settles the will, awaiting the season and the year, all is auspicious; but if one hopes for swiftness, it will not go smoothly. It is also said: once yin is in its upright place, the way of earth is thereby attained — the image of human affairs dwelling in their estate. Seeking office, looking for wealth, managing fields and silkworms — all are auspicious. Marriage is hard at first and easy later. The traveler should arrive. Staying at home is peaceful and good. Official matters do not come to pass. The imprisoned will be released only through exertion.
he: The far traveler should arrive; the pregnant will bear a son; in official matters and imprisonment, one is released by an amnesty. The sick will not die. All affairs are auspicious.
chen: Heaven and man are both yang, and the way of earth is gentle and fair; yin has not yet reached its fullness, and above and below respond to each other. Hence the saying.
liu: Dwelling at peace and managing the estate, firm and yielding attain each other. Not longing for what is outside, one truly receives blessing. In this cast two yang are above and one yin dwells below; the positions of the Three Powers are all attained, hence the image of being both rich and honored. One should keep and preserve this, and not make insatiable demands — then it is auspicious. The household and marriage succeed. Official matters are unhindered. The traveler comes home. Office sought is already obtained, though the affairs of it are not yet managed. On hearing of sorrow, one is not sorrowful. Illness, though not yet healed, is harmless.

name: Hexagram of Auspicious Celebration
note: Pure yang holding position; Qian, Heaven, northwest
xiang: Lofty and illustrious, the household has its gold and silk. Goods are ready and affairs are done; without seeking, all is gained of itself.
yan: Since there is gold and silk, there is no need to seek. Staying at home is auspicious; the traveler has not returned. It is also said: Heaven gives birth to the myriad things, and its principle grows ever more abundant; without reliance on management, all is accomplished of itself. This hexagram is pure yang; marriage is not harmonious, the imprisoned are guiltless, fields and silkworms are both profitable, and all else is auspicious.
he: The traveler is about to arrive; the pregnant will bear a son. Trade is profitable; in official matters one meets with an amnesty; in catching thieves, one is sure to capture them.
chen: All three positions are yang, and the lower position alone is flourishing — the image of the way of earth filled and solid. Above and below are both lacking. Hence the saying.
liu: Lofty and illustrious — pure yang throughout. The household has its gold and silk — the way of earth is radiant. Goods are ready and affairs are done — the force is abundant and strong; without seeking, all is gained of itself — truly it is thriving and prosperous. In this cast there are three yang with the lower position flourishing; the way of earth brings forth its produce, and so gold and silk are full and goods are ready and affairs are done. The abundant yang is rooted below, and the lesser yang rises above, like a tree whose root is vigorous and whose fruit is plentiful; hence the image of gaining all without seeking. The diviner who obtains it, in seeking affairs, finds all auspicious, and managing an estate is most profitable. In war there is great victory, and in pursuing fugitives one is sure to capture them. Only in a lawsuit does one win at the cost of wealth. Divining about illness is inauspicious. To flee or go into hiding cannot succeed.

name: Hexagram of Wealth and Abundance
note: Yin flourishing in its place; Xun, Wind, southeast
xiang: Wealth abundant, honor at its height; the way of Heaven turns and shifts. Rise and fall with the course of fortune; wax and wane with the season. Sons and grandsons after, by the ten thousand and the hundred million.
yan: Whoever dwells in wealth and honor without forgetting poverty and lowliness leaves his name to posterity; but if he cannot be humble and retiring, he is sure to bring about his own overthrow. The traveler is far away and returns only after a long while. It is also said: from two to four, the way of earth is again completed, and the principle of wealth and honor here reaches its utmost. To dwell in fullness is sure to suffer decrease; to dwell on high is sure to be in danger. Hence it says 'turns and shifts.' If one waxes and wanes with fullness and emptiness, and does not go against the season's course, he is sure to preserve his body and keep his name whole, and to let his blessings flow down upon his descendants. This hexagram favors humility and withdrawal; the imprisoned are hard to release, awaited people come a little late, and the traveler has not yet arrived.
he: The sick recover slowly; one should sacrifice to the heavenly gods and seek blessings. Marriage is auspicious. In accumulating wealth one should not be greedy and add to it further. A far journey is not fitting, and may bring quarrels and slander; in official matters, seek one who enforces the law to resolve them.
chen: Two yang are above, and yin flourishes below; the way of earth is brimming full, and does not encroach upon what is above. Hence the saying.
liu: Wealth abundant and honor at its height — the household estate is complete. Rising and falling with the course of fortune, one preserves one's fullness. Sons and grandsons should not contend. In this cast two yang are above and old yin dwells below; above and below gain their places, and there is position and substance — the image of wealth and honor at their utmost, with nothing that could be added. Therefore one should follow the course and the season, know contentment, and act without presumption; then one can preserve what is already accomplished, and sons and grandsons will maintain it without loss. Divining about marriage is auspicious. Seeking office, looking for wealth, and hoping for affairs are all already gained; one should not hope beyond this. For the traveler, staying put is auspicious. In official matters seek reconciliation; if it recurs, there will be regret. Illness is about to heal. In battle one should not act rashly or in haste; when one sees what is attainable, stop — that is auspicious. In seeking a person, one will not be believed. In all affairs, when they reach the extreme they are sure to turn back; what is auspicious will bring misfortune, and what is inauspicious will bring good fortune.
shi:
A light boat meets the waves and flies along;
in a hundred affairs, your pursuit is right on time.
If you share the road with a noble man,
from this, a hundred blessings will follow of themselves.

name: Hexagram of Delight and Joy
note: Yin and yang in union; Gen, Mountain, northeast
xiang: Husband and wife hold each other dear, with no other person between. Seated knee to knee, there is ever delight and joy.
yan: Firm and yielding respond to each other — the image of harmony and delight; all affairs are in accord, marriage is very auspicious, and trade is profitable.
he: The dwelling is peaceful and safe. Whatever is sought is gained, and all affairs follow the heart. Fields and silkworms yield a great harvest. Official matters disperse, the sick recover, and the traveler returns. It is an omen of good fortune and profit.
chen: Yin and yang attain each other — the image of husband and wife. Hence the saying.
liu: Husband and wife hold each other dear — the household is fitting. Seated knee to knee in joy, they delight themselves together. In this cast, though there is no lower position, the yang above and the yin in the middle form an incomparable match, with no harm between them. The diviner, in dwelling at home and in marriage, finds all affairs harmonious and favorable — auspicious. But only small matters may be done, not great ones.
shi:
Twofold joy from the heavens above;
your eyes open together at once.
Freed from loneliness and lingering delay,
you unfold your rare talents at will.

name: Hexagram of Delighting in the Way
note: Yang firm, yin gentle; Li, Fire, due south
xiang: Outwardly firm and inwardly gentle, harmoniously united and complete in itself. Nurture your nature and preserve your life, and wander together with the spirit.
yan: What is sought goes astray; one can only cultivate virtue and preserve the body. The sick have not recovered; one should sacrifice and seek blessings. The traveler has not returned, advancement in office does not come, official matters do not succeed, and the imprisoned are hard to release. It is also said: marriage is auspicious, the pregnant will bear a son, and the sick should pray to the spirits.
he: Marriage is auspicious, the pregnant will bear a son, trade is profitable, and a campaign is greatly auspicious. It is also said: yin dwells in a yang position, hence it is outwardly firm. One should not force one's advance; one should preserve life and nourish one's nature — the image of self-nourishment.
chen: Above and below are both yang, while the way of man is weak and yin, unable to accomplish anything; there is the image of embracing gentleness and nurturing one's nature. Yet yin dwells in a yang position, now startled, now delighted; hence the saying.
liu: Outwardly firm and inwardly gentle, one should be in accord with others. One should be fond of planning and careful in affairs, so as to preserve one's person whole. Wandering together with the spirit is not inauspicious either. In this cast one yin dwells between two yang, hence the image of outward firmness and inward gentleness. Yin in a yang position should not act; therefore one should be harmonious, circumspect, and careful, and so preserve oneself — auspicious. Divining about illness, there is a baleful influence; sacrifice and prayer are auspicious. A lawsuit does not come to pass. Marriage and trade are auspicious. An army sent out will not fight. The imprisoned are hard to release. Things heard are mostly false and deceptive; one should not scheme in the dark.
shi:
Two people in harmony show their delight;
hopes sought and plans devised can be achieved.
Even if a green serpent comes to trouble and disturb,
in the end it harms neither profit nor fame.

name: Hexagram of Terror and Fright
note: Yin at its extreme, yang alone; Gen, Mountain, northeast
xiang: The cock crows in daylight, mounting the roof and craning its neck. The hen is below the wall, startled by a wildcat. With a desperate cry it comes to her aid, and so she escapes injury and ruin.
yan: In all affairs, though at first one is in a sorry plight, in the end there is nothing to fear; a hundred affairs are first broken and then completed. The traveler has not arrived, and illness should be treated early. It is also said: the response above is at the beginning, but is cut off in the middle and cannot come to the rescue; hence the fright. Yet dwelling on high and treading danger, one in the end overcomes the strong adversary; with a desperate cry one rushes to the rescue and escapes disaster and ruin. The cock belongs to yang and the hen to yin; of all the robbers of chickens, none is worse than the wildcat. This hexagram is of worry and fright; official matters do not come to pass, and the imprisoned are released only through a person of influence.
he: On a far journey one meets with robbers; seeking office, marriage, and trade are all unfavorable. Borrowing and seeking are difficult, what is sought goes against one's wishes, and fields and silkworms yield no harvest. In every affair there is first worry, then joy.
chen: Yang governs safety and yin governs danger; two yin are in the middle, and one yang is not enough to rely upon, while there are again two yin below. Hence the saying.
liu: One cock and two hens — there is sure to be contention. The firm and vigorous is above, and the yielding cannot encroach upon it. Moving smoothly with a true response, one is kept from ruin. In this cast the lesser yang dwells in the honored position, while the two yin below both wish to follow it. The upper responds to the first, but is cut off in the middle; hence the image of the cock mounting the roof and the hen below being startled by the wildcat. Yet yang is above in the ruling position, and the central yin is not yet strong; hence in the end there is rescue and no injury or ruin. Affairs divined are laborious — first danger, then safety; first worry, then joy. The traveler returns but meets an obstacle midway. A campaign has its frights. Illness should be treated by a physician at once. Seeking office, marriage, and hoped-for affairs are all obstructed by people, and one must rely upon someone of influence; in all, first difficulty, then attainment.
shi:
In the dark, beware the hidden pit;
on river and sea, wind and waves arise.
Looking back upon the place of joy,
it has turned instead into a bitter illness.

name: Hexagram of the Bountiful Year
note: Yin departing, yang arriving; Li, Fire, due south
xiang: In the first month, at the hour of the horse, the year stands in Daliang. The east wind melts the ice, favoring your fields and mulberry groves. At year's end the harvest is abundant, and joy brims and overflows.
yan: What is sought is auspicious in the year, month, day, or hour of the Rat, Horse, Hare, or Cock, though the response comes a little late. Outside these years, months, days, or hours it will not succeed. Divining about fields and silkworms, nothing is unfavorable. It is also said: it is the image of yin departing and yang advancing; when the year stands in the Cock it is called Daliang. The proverb says: 'When the Year Star is in the west, beg for water and receive wine,' speaking of abundance. In this hexagram fields and silkworms are auspicious; divining about office, it is not yet attained. In holding office there is no worry, and the sick have no suffering.
he: Traveling by water or by land, and marriage in harmony, are greatly auspicious. The traveler is detained, and the imprisoned are released slowly.
chen: The upper and middle positions respond as yin and yang, and three yang are in the earth — the image of the way of earth filled and solid. Hence the saying.
liu: Heaven and man are in harmony, and yin follows yang. The land is rich and ample, favoring fields and mulberry groves. At the juncture of the Horse and the Cock, the profit cannot be withstood. In this cast the lesser yang is above and the lesser yin in the middle follows it; the positions of Heaven and man are attained. The abundant yang dwells in the position of earth, so that above is harmony and below is richness; hence fields and mulberry groves are favored. The first month means the first line. Daliang is the Cock. In the body of the cast, the lower three form Li; Li is the Horse. The middle two form Dui; Dui is the Cock. Yan Youming says: 'When the Year Star is in the Cock, beg for water and receive wine,' speaking of richness. All affairs divined come out as one wishes, and the response lies in the year, month, day, or hour of the Horse or the Cock, or in the western quarter.

name: Hexagram of Small Caution
note: Yin flourishing, overcoming yang; Gen, Mountain, northeast
xiang: Calamity arises from below; be on guard against servants and lads. Secret plots join in the dark, seeking to lay hold of hands and feet.
yan: Though yang has gained its place, a host of yin plots against it; hence it says 'servants and lads,' for the secret plot seeks to do harm. One should be wary of those on one's left and right. In this hexagram all affairs are worrisome, but do not lead to great misfortune. Official matters come to pass, but the imprisoned are hard to release, because yang is weak.
he: The traveler meets with robbers, and those at home have worries. Servants and maids do harm. At gatherings there are quarrels; affairs sought do not succeed; and the sick have been cursed by their inferiors.
chen: Although the upper and middle positions attain each other, below there are four yin excessively strong, and the way of man is already weak — the image of a host of petty ones encroaching. Hence the saying.
liu: Lone yang is above, and its force is few and weak. Yin flourishes below, and there is worry about maids and servants. In this cast one yang dwells above while a host of yin is below, and the central position is lesser yin, soft and weak and unable to restrain what is below; hence the image of calamity arising from below, and of guarding against servants and lads. All affairs divined are unfavorable. This differs from the sixth cast, which also has one yang above but divines differently: there the lower position is lesser yin, which has the will to follow above but is blocked in the middle; here it is old yin, whose force runs wanton below while the middle cannot restrain it — like a household of a weak husband and a young wife, where bold slaves and fierce maids will not obey their master's orders. Its misfortune can be known.
shi:
The cauldron is lost — where is the firewood?
Beware lest flame-bringing disaster reach your house.
Wealth and goods will in the end be lost;
servants and lads too must be guarded against.

name: Hexagram of Gradual Fulfillment
note: Two yang in their places; Qian, Heaven, northwest
xiang: Dwelling in one's proper place, affairs attain one's wish. Settle the will and calm the mind, and blessings and emolument are just now arriving. Celebration and congratulation abound, and it will long be to my profit.
yan: Three yang are at the center, and one yang responds to them; order is attained, and all affairs are auspicious.
he: All affairs follow the heart. Marriage is harmonious. Official matters dissolve. Dwelling at home is rich and joyful. In office one is promoted to high rank. The sick should not worry, for there is someone to seek a physician. Wealth sought is gained. The traveler returns before he is even expected. The ten thousand affairs are greatly auspicious.
chen: The way of man is flourishing with yang, and above and below there is no conflict; the will to live springs up abundantly. Hence the saying.
liu: The way of yang is just now pervading, and one dwells in his proper place. Above and below there is no treachery, and blessing and profit are preserved. This cast attains its place; all affairs divined are auspicious.
shi:
Whether you hasten or go slowly, there is a course of its own;
the moon sinks into the western sea, the sun rises in the east.
When fortune comes, why toil the heart and strength?
The wind carries the river tide, clear for ten thousand li.

name: Hexagram of Attaining One's Aim
note: Pure yang holding position; Qian, Heaven, northwest
xiang: Clearly one attains his aim, meeting squarely with his season. Wealth comes in plenty for his use, and there is no lack of those to serve.
yan: One's will and wish are gained, goods are sufficient for use, and there are also those to serve. It is also said: pure yang presides over affairs — the image of attaining one's aim. Set your heart on the common good, and wealth and resources will be ample and complete. Han Fei says: when King Wen attacked Chong and reached the mound of Yellow Bamboo, the laces of his leather leggings came undone; he looked about and saw that all around him were worthy men whom he could not order about, and so he tied them himself. This is the noble man, the worthy man, holding to the way of utmost impartiality.
he: In office, emolument is abundant; the far traveler arrives. The sick recover of themselves. The imprisoned are released. The pregnant will bear a son. Trade is profitable. What is sought brings a great gain.
chen: Three yang are in the middle, the way of man is wholly achieved, and above and below there is no breach. Hence the saying.
liu: The dragon's virtue is in the true center, and one greatly attains his season. Above and below cooperate and follow, sufficient for great action. In this cast the abundant yang dwells in the central position, attaining its aim and its season, while the lesser yang above and below are of one mind with it; why fear that wealth should fall short or servants be lacking? The diviner who obtains it, whatever he seeks, nothing cannot be gained — it is a greatly auspicious cast.

name: Hexagram of Affairs Accomplished
note: Yin and yang in harmony; Xun, Wind, southeast
xiang: What before did not suit one's wishes is now in accord with one's will. The ten thousand affairs attain their order; act with clarity and openness.
yan: Now that one's aim begins to be fulfilled, one should take loyalty and openness as the root, and not pursue private ends. The traveler returns. The sick recover. It is also said: the positions of the Three Powers are upright, yin and yang are in accord, and the way of the noble man here reaches peace; one is promoted in office and gains length of years. Trade is profitable. All affairs are auspicious.
he: Marriage is harmonious. In using troops there is great victory. Fields and silkworms bring profit. The poor find redress. The imprisoned are freed. Affairs sought succeed, and a far journey arrives. Acting with clarity and openness, the ten thousand affairs all follow their proper principle.
chen: Three yang are in the middle, the way of man is already flourishing, and above and below respond to each other in turn. Hence the saying.
liu: What before did not suit one's wishes — the yielding is within. Yang flourishes and acts outwardly, and the season opens into peace. With integrity and selflessness, its way is the great earth. In this cast the positions of the Three Powers are upright, yin and yang are in accord, and the way of the noble man is just now pervading; one should not be secret and selfish, but should do what is upright, great, and open. The diviner who obtains it — greatly auspicious.
shi:
Toiling in the dust, I have long awaited the season;
in the lonely window, who knows my solitude?
When fortune meets one who bears a sword and turns to look,
profit attained and fame achieved — there is always a season for it.

name: Hexagram of Talent Prevailing
note: Many yang flourishing below; Qian, Heaven, northwest
xiang: A throng of worthy gentlemen, their fine virtue radiant and bright. They meet one another with delight, and long enjoy happiness without calamity.
yan: The number of yang is manifold, hence 'a throng of gentlemen.' One makes one's way in the world by talent, and there should be a noble person to help. Only at year's end does one gain his strength, and not for a single season only. The sick recover. The traveler returns. All affairs are auspicious. For a scholar wishing to see kings and lords and to seek reputation, it is even better.
he: Office sought is obtained. The traveler arrives. Trade, fields, and silkworms are profitable, and marriage is auspicious. The sick recover. Official matters do not come to pass. This hexagram is greatly auspicious.
chen: The way of three yang is flourishing and capable of action, and the way of earth likewise obtains the fullness of abundant yang. Wherever one dwells, all is secure. Hence the saying.
liu: A throng of worthy gentlemen — they follow what is above. Meeting one another with delight, in going forward there is honor. In this cast one yang holds the true position above, while the middle and lower are both three yang — like a lord of men with firm and bright virtue, whom a host of worthies follows. A commoner who obtains it becomes a person of rank; it is the image of good friends helping one another. Divining about seeking office, meeting the noble, marriage, and trade — all are auspicious. In using troops one gains worthy men; in seeking affairs one should obtain the help of others — auspicious.

name: Hexagram of Unfettered Wandering
note: Yin and yang in their places; Xun, Wind, southeast
xiang: Riding the dragon and driving the steeds, one roams abroad through the four quarters. The heart is glad and the mind at ease; the joy of the journey knows no bound.
yan: One follows one's heart's desire — east, west, south, or north, and nothing more. In all affairs there is nothing that is not accomplished. The traveler has not arrived. The sick recover. The Book of Changes says: 'at the proper season he rides the six dragons to drive the heavens.' And again: 'like herding horses, one of the earth's kind, he travels the earth without bound.'
he: Catching thieves and recovering lost things both succeed; the pregnant will bear a son, and trade is profitable. A proposal of marriage will of itself be accepted. Fields and silkworms are to one's liking. The imprisoned have no worry; all affairs are brought to success.
chen: The upper and middle are both yang, and below there are four yin; yin and yang attain each other, and moreover the way of man is in full vigor, sufficient to command the host of yin. Hence the saying.
liu: Riding the dragon and driving the steeds — below follows and bears up. Roaming abroad through the four quarters, none dares to withstand me. In this cast one yang dwells above, while the middle and lower are all in place; the three yang are the dragon and the four yin are the steeds, each attaining its place to be of use to me. Hence it is fitting to roam abroad through the four quarters and take pleasure without bound. The diviner who obtains it should greatly press forward. Only when asking about a traveler, he has not yet returned, though abroad he too is attaining his aim.

name: Hexagram of Ghosts Lying in Wait
note: Yin stealing the central position; Gen, Mountain, northeast
xiang: Food does not enter the mouth, breath does not issue from the nose. The heart and belly are vexed and knotted, so that one cannot sleep.
yan: Yang is weak and yin is strong; a host of yin dwells within and does not submit to yang, and so harm and suffering are brought about.
he: For the sick it is inauspicious. The imprisoned are hard to release; in reason one should reproach oneself and not blame others. On a far journey one meets with robbers. Boatmen meet with the harm of wind and water; all affairs are inauspicious.
chen: Four yin are just now flourishing, and one yang does not respond — the image of ghostly airs filling everything. Hence the saying.
liu: One yang and four yin — the will does not get through. The heart and belly are vexed and knotted — illness is within. In this cast a host of yin occupies the position of man, while lone yang is above with none to be its companion; above and below are not in accord, and the breath does not flow. Be careful to guard against hidden thieves; in travel there is worry about wind, water, and robbers; all affairs divined are inauspicious.

name: Hexagram of Worry and Peril
note: Two yang divided by yin; Li, Fire, due south
xiang: Above is single and below is solitary, plotted against by the treacherous. The illness in the heart and belly cannot be removed all at once. Await the arrival of bright spring, and then one may be at ease again.
yan: One constantly harbors dread and fear, apprehensive of worry and peril. Yet one is glad to gain the rescue and protection of a noble person, and in the end there is no blame. The sick recover only after two or three months. It is also said: two yang are cut off by doubled yin and cannot come to the rescue — like a treacherous minister stealing the government, who first strikes the petty men; this is the image of worry and peril. In all affairs there is little fortune, and the traveler meets with distress.
he: Managing the estate is not auspicious, and one is plotted against by thieves. The sick recover slowly. The imprisoned are not yet released, and affairs move slowly and haltingly; this hexagram is mildly inauspicious.
chen: Four yin are in the middle, and the way of man is at the extreme of weakness; the faint yang above and below cannot give support. Hence the saying.
liu: Above is single and below is solitary — yin flourishes in the middle. The petty man obstructs and blocks, and the will does not get through. Holding to the right and awaiting the season, one can be preserved to the end. In this cast above and below are each one yang, while four yin occupy the middle — the image of petty men banding together and the upright way being blocked. All affairs divined have obstructions and are unfavorable. One should guard oneself with what is right, so as to avoid calamity. This resembles the fifth cast, yet here there is worry: there the lesser yin dwelt in the middle with a will to draw near to yang, and so it was the image of harmony and self-completeness. In this cast the four yin band together, and their force is numerous and strong; removing them is very hard, and so one awaits the month of yang, when one's aid arrives, to resolve the distress.
shi:
Established yet not settled in body,
fright and worry are ever in the heart.
How many times have I met danger and hindrance?
On what day shall I meet one who knows my tone?

name: Hexagram of Guarding Virtue
note: Yin at its extreme, reversing position; Gen, Mountain, northeast
xiang: Heaven and earth are wide and slack; the petty man does as he pleases. Bans and orders go unheeded, and thieves spy upon my cottage.
