yan: A host of yin is just now flourishing, and lone yang cannot spring forth; the way of the petty man grows, and the way of the noble man declines. One should lose goods and wealth. The head of the household suffers illness, which heals only by autumn. This hexagram greatly favors holding to the right and does not favor seeking affairs. The traveler has no set time, and pursuers will not make their capture.
he: The sick have not recovered, and taking medicine is of no help. Official matters are not light. Wealth sought brings thin profit. Dwelling at home, be careful to guard against thieves; this hexagram is inauspicious.
chen: Four yin are in the middle and two yin below, and one yang cannot restrain them — a time when the petty man attains his aim. Hence the saying.
liu: Heaven and earth are wide and slack — laws and orders have grown lax. Thieves spy upon my cottage — one is blinded and cannot see. The noble man's grief is the petty man's joy. In this cast a host of yin against one yang, the central position flourishing with yin; the lower, which should respond to the upper, is blocked in the middle and instead joins with it — the noble man's dwelling is seized by thieves. The diviner should guard against thieves. Dwelling at home, managing the estate, trading, seeking office, using troops, and traveling — every affair is inauspicious. Only in flight and concealment is there fortune.
shi:
A host of fiends fills the six directions;
sun and moon are veiled by wind and dust.
Though from now on you examine yourself and cultivate virtue,
you may still hardly escape calamity.

name: Hexagram of Issuing Commands
note: Yin dwelling at the center; Li, Fire, due south
xiang: The lord commands his officers and men to punish the rebels, the treacherous and fierce. They take up spears and set their halberds forth, and greatly do they follow the command.
yan: One should be driven by others, and should also drive others; if one acts on one's own authority, all is ruined. The sick have a ghostly influence, which should be exorcised. The traveler has not returned; one should hasten to fetch him — auspicious. Divining about punishing rebels and capturing fugitives, one is sure to prevail. It is also said: within, one is a traitor; without, one is a fierce foe. This hexagram favors punitive expeditions and the capture of fugitives, and brings great victory besides. Trade is profitable. Office sought is also obtained. Fields, silkworms, and marriage are all auspicious.
he: When the sovereign removes the fierce, there is sure to be one he drives forth; official matters are resolved, and no affair is inauspicious.
chen: Four yin are in the middle — a time when thieves and robbers run rampant. Yet three yang are below, sufficient to give the multitude peace; there is the image of an army going out to punish the guilty. Hence the saying.
liu: The treacherous yin is in the middle, seeking to spy upon the upright. The lord commands its punishment, and the army's strength is abundant. Taking up spears and setting halberds forth, one smites the treacherous. In this cast one yang holds the true position above, while three yang spring up abundantly below, and four yin occupy the middle; though they would obstruct, the two yang join their virtue, and the hidden yin is already exposed. Hence the image of the lord commanding his officers and men to punish and remove the treacherous and fierce. Divining about going to war and capturing fugitives, there is great victory. The sick, once treated, recover at once; the litigant, once his case is heard, prevails. The traveler is unharmed; obstacles can be passed through; all affairs are auspicious.

name: Hexagram of Impending Loss
note: Yin at its extreme, overcoming yang; Gen, Mountain, northeast
xiang: Jackals and tigers roar and snarl, and drenching rain pours down. In battle there is no victory; the troops are weak and the soldiers dull. Overborne by the enemy, many are lost and slain.
yan: Overcoming one and profiting another — none of this follows reason. In all affairs there is great difficulty; the traveler should return. Midway there is terror; one should not go to punish rebels. It is also said: the yin qi grows ever stronger, and the way of the lord declines day by day; jackals and tigers — the outer foes — press in from all four sides, and the enemy is hard to overcome.
he: The border commander guarding the frontier is sure to be robbed by bandits; though he keeps to the high ground, he is struck across by floodwater. The sick are in deep and grave distress, and the imprisoned are held firm. Disputes and lawsuits, the use of troops, trade, seeking office, fields and silkworms — a hundred affairs are all unfavorable. This is the situation of a losing army.
chen: The yin kind greatly rises; wild beasts, thieves, and robbers join together to harm the people. One yang cannot restrain them, and ruin and defeat are sure to appear. Hence the saying.
liu: Jackals roar and waters overflow — the way of yang is solitary; great traitors join in league, and the peril cannot be propped up. In this cast yang perches upon accumulated yin, hence the image of jackals and tigers roaring and drenching rain pouring down. All affairs divined are inauspicious, and the use of troops is most to be avoided. Only in praying for rain in a great drought is it sure to serve.
shi:
Shooting at the pheasant, in the end it is hard to take it;
cherishing a treasure, you have not gained the wealth.
In ventures and in hopes that press forward alike,
your very steps stir up danger and disaster.
Again: your force is slight, beware of the enemy's raid;
loss, theft, and the peril of fire come of it.
Human affairs are all like this —
the season of Heaven is not yet in accord with the moment.

name: Hexagram of Drifting Adrift
note: Faint yin reversing position; Kun, Earth, southwest
xiang: From Heaven an image is set up, but the qi still floats and drifts. Nothing can yet be fixed and settled; east and west it wanders and flows. Much does not follow one's wishes; all is vast and endless and slow.
yan: From one to two, the number only just multiplies; yet the foundation and traces are only beginning, and the way of man is not yet established. Hence the image of drifting and unsettledness, of vastness and endlessness; much does not follow one's wishes.
he: Human affairs are not yet fulfilled — an omen of non-completion.
chen: Two is the beginning of yin qi, dwelling in the position of Heaven, like a drifting cloud that is never fixed. Hence the saying.
liu: From Heaven an image is set up — its way is faint. East and west it wanders and flows — the foundation is not yet formed. In this cast human affairs are not settled, and undertakings do not succeed.
shi:
Seeking emolument is truly of no profit;
and striving and seeking also have their hindrance.
Even if you gain success and delight,
when you see the tiger you must still be on guard.

name: Hexagram of Emptiness and Loss
note: Yin and yang overturned; Zhen, Thunder, due east
xiang: Entering the water to cut timber, climbing the mountain to catch fish — labor is lost and strength is spent, with empty hands and an idle mouth.
yan: The position of man is lacking, and Heaven and Earth are overturned; establishing merit and creating affairs both come to nothing. Hence it is said: entering the water to cut timber, climbing the mountain to catch fish — in the end nothing can be taken. In this hexagram marriage is greatly inauspicious, and the sick are hard to save, because yin and yang are turned upside down.
he: The traveler does not come. The sick are at their gravest. Marriage does not unite. Official matters are hard to resolve, and seeking wealth and seeking office are both to be feared as unobtainable. This hexagram is greatly unfavorable.
chen: The way of man is already empty, and above and below yin and yang are opposed; there is nothing that can be taken. Hence the saying.
liu: Entering the water to cut timber is to walk against the way. With empty hands and an idle mouth, there is nothing with which to live. In this cast yin and yang are overturned and there is no position of man; there is the image of climbing the mountain to catch fish and entering the water to cut timber, saying that one's heart's desire cannot be gained and that all affairs are inauspicious.
shi:
The precious moon wanes even at the full;
the long river is muddy and yet clear.
Even if there is no blame or harm,
still one may fear to stir a needless fright.

name: Hexagram of Discord
note: Two yin not in accord; Kun, Earth, southwest
xiang: Two women with no husband quarrel and dwell apart. Going out and coming in by different roads, they separate their chambers and houses.
yan: Within and without are both yin, and their wills do not accord — like two women with no husband, who by nature come to quarrel; the dwelling grows still more inauspicious, and marriage does not unite. In this hexagram all affairs are inauspicious, because there is a yin with no master. Hence it is said: two women dwelling together, their wills do not accord. To obtain this hexagram is greatly inauspicious.
he: There is an air of parting, like one moving house without moving wholly away. Official matters are hard to avoid, the sick recover slowly, and the traveler has not returned. Marching troops, seeking wealth, and various affairs are all unfavorable. In all affairs there is sure to be division and dispersal.
chen: The central position has no person, and the two yin above and below do not respond to each other — like two women dwelling together, alike in form but different in will. Hence the saying.
liu: Above and below are two yin — there is a woman but no husband. Going out and coming in by different roads, the household within is empty. In this cast above and below are both yin and the middle has no master; hence the image of two women with no husband, their wills not in accord, separating their chambers. For the diviner, all affairs go contrary, and what is sought is inauspicious.
shi:
Bright clouds fly apart, and the water flows east;
in the lonely dusk, affairs are fit for sorrow.
Even if at present there is not a single trouble,
still vexation will follow you until mid-autumn.

name: Hexagram of the Double Abyss
note: Lone yang out of place; Zhen, Thunder, due east
xiang: Two people follow one another, wishing to travel and avoid the danger. They meet misfortune and fall into the well, their strength and sinew to no purpose.
yan: Wishing to avoid the harm of yin, one loses one's place; like meeting misfortune and falling into the well, the hands and feet remain but to no purpose, and the sinew and strength are spent. A hundred affairs do not succeed. In building and managing, much does not suit one's wishes; a far journey is most inauspicious.
he: One wishes to act, but there is no place to apply one's strength; what is sought is not gained, and what is done is hard to complete. Divining about illness is all the more inauspicious; seeking a physician only makes it worse. The traveler has a calamity. It is an image of great misfortune.
chen: Two yin are above, and the central position is already void; three yang are below, as at the bottom of a well, with no place to apply their strength. Hence the saying.
liu: Wishing to travel and avoid danger, the hearts are full of mutual doubt; meeting misfortune and falling into the well, how lamentable. In this cast lesser yin is above and firm yang dwells below, and their wills do not accord; hence they first doubt each other and in the end both fall in. Yan says: wishing to avoid the harm of yin, one loses one's place; like meeting misfortune and falling into the well, the hands and feet remain but to no purpose, and the sinew and strength are spent — all affairs are inauspicious.
shi:
The household is itself much afflicted;
secret merit is best pressed forward.
Amid the crossing lines of written words,
a lotus blooms within the fire.

name: Hexagram of Lai Ge
note: Yin qi overflowing; Kun, Earth, southwest
xiang: Frost and snow fall thick and fast, drenching my robe and coat. The north wind blows upon me, and I cannot turn and go home.
yan: The yin qi overflows, and within and without there is no master; wind and frost drift one about, and the road home is dim and far. This hexagram has many faults; for the traveler it is all the more inauspicious, and seeking office and buying and selling mostly do not succeed.
he: In all affairs nothing follows the heart; there are quarrels, slander, and backbiting, and one should be most careful of them. Guard further against the loss of wealth. In office, retiring to idleness avoids disaster; in a hundred affairs, be all the more careful.
chen: Above and below are both yin, and the central position has no person; the petty man runs rampant, and the noble man has no place to lodge his body. Hence the saying. Lai Ge is the name of a wicked man — namely Elai Ge.
liu: Frost and snow fall thick and fast — yin qi gathers. One cannot turn and go home — there is no household. In this cast all affairs are inauspicious, and a far journey is especially unfitting.
shi:
Where joy reaches its height, sorrow is born;
the gold of last night is gone.
The plan for what comes after is already lost,
and the road home does not run smooth.

name: Hexagram of Belated Good Fortune
note: Yin and yang overturned; Zhen, Thunder, due east
xiang: Entrusting a matter to another, day after day you await his mind. Only now, at last, do you gain good tidings and joy. Though the affair lingers long, in the end your wish is fulfilled.
yan: Though the positions are inverted and disordered, in their interaction there is aid; entrusting a matter to another, one in the end gains its good fortune. Because one's own position is solitary and slight, one cannot arrive on one's own, and so it is through lingering that fortune comes. This hexagram responds slowly but is auspicious.
he: Entrusting a matter to another, do not be weary of the lateness; then it follows the heart, and there is celebration without; in all affairs, good fortune comes late.
chen: Yang governs swiftness and yin governs delay; the upper and middle positions fundamentally respond to each other, yet the yin above is gentle and responds to me somewhat slowly. Hence the saying.
liu: Entrusting a matter to another, one's seeking is not yet obtained. Lingering long, one's wish is fulfilled; in the end there is attainment. In this cast yin and yang, though adjacent, have their upper and lower crossed; one's own position is solitary and slight, and one cannot arrive at once, and so only after long does one get through. In all affairs there is first worry, then joy; in the end what is sought is fulfilled; one should not be hasty or impatient.
shi:
The road ahead will have its day of rich abundance;
what is planned and entrusted will in the end suit my heart.
And when a noble person turns a favoring eye,
in one season the spring's beauty fills the whole courtyard.

name: Hexagram of Divine Protection
note: Yin dwelling in a yang position; Dui, Metal, due west
xiang: Taiyi leads forth the troops, the Jade Maiden at his side. Wuxian sweeps clean before him, and the inauspicious is cast away.
yan: The head of the household is ill, and there is a female ghost doing mischief, which should be exorcised. In all affairs there is much that is dark, and because of it the traveler does not return. It is also said: among the honored heavenly spirits, there are Taiyi, the Jade Maiden, and Wuxian to assist him; Wuxian was a worthy minister of Yin. In this hexagram, prayer brings blessing; but seeking office, hoping for affairs, trade, and marriage are unfavorable.
he: The traveler should arrive; there is no suffering from quarrels, and official matters in the end hold no harm. One gains the strength of others; one should seek blessings and remove misfortune, and then what is done will succeed.
chen: Two is fundamentally a yin number, yet on the contrary it dwells in the position of Heaven — the image of a heavenly spirit. Below it responds to one in the middle and one below, and one is sure to obtain the blessing of the heavenly spirit. Hence the saying.
liu: Taiyi leads forth the troops and removes the inauspicious. Yang arrives and yin is solitary; the baleful does not last. In this cast yin, though dwelling above, has two yang gaining a companion below; there is the force of one mind expelling evil, while the yin above is, on the contrary, used by me. Hence the omen of Taiyi leading the troops, with the Jade Maiden at his side and Wuxian exorcising beforehand. Affairs divined, though there are doubts and difficulties, in the end gain the help of friends and come to success. The sick, once exorcised, recover at once. The traveler returns. In battle there is great victory.

name: Hexagram of Impending Defeat
note: Two yin restraining yang; Kan, Water, due north
xiang: Two women and one husband, above and below contending to drive him. The yin qi rides over the yang, and so all is spent and drained to emptiness.
yan: Man and woman overcome each other; though married at first, they part afterward. The traveler, though he returns, meets with robbers on the way. It is also said: without, one is not the Jade Maiden; within, one turns against Taiyi. With one yang subjected to two yin, it is the image of exhaustion and waste. The sick are gravely ill.
he: What is sought brings no benefit, and what is done is not harmonious. The traveler has not arrived. Fields and silkworms bring disappointment. Official matters are hard to resolve. A hundred affairs are greatly inauspicious.
chen: The way of man is solitary and weak, and the two yin above and below both wish to advance upon it. Two women and one husband is the image of licentious concealment; the faint yang cannot prevail.
liu: Two women and one husband — yang sinks into yin. Resisting the essence and repelling the spirit, one follows after lewdness. Thus all is spent and drained to emptiness, with fear of sinking into ruin. In this cast one yang is sunk between two yin, and both yin and yang are young; drowning in the desire for union, the yang cannot rouse itself and is ridden by the yin, and so it is sure to come to exhaustion and waste. Whatever is divined and obtained is inauspicious.

name: Hexagram of Ordering Chaos
note: Yin stealing the yang position; Dui, Lake, due west
xiang: Heaven darkens and clouds rise; yang arises from below. The noble man sets chaos in order, and the petty man fears his chastisement.
yan: Yin steals the yang position, like the rising of clouds; abundant yang is below, about to ascend to the ninth-five. Removing the rebellious and forbidding the violent, the host of evil dissolves of itself — a small chastisement and a great warning. This hexagram, for one who governs men and controls affairs, and for a senior official who obtains it, is the best; in a hundred affairs there is first worry, then good fortune.
he: What is sought is not gained, and what is done is not completed. In holding office and ordering chaos, the petty man fears punishment. The sick have not recovered. The traveler, though far, finds no profit and there is slander.
chen: Two yin are above and abundant yang is below — the image of intersecting peace. Three dwells in the position of earth; the petty man has no place in the world, and hence the saying.
liu: Heaven darkens and clouds rise — the dragon leaps from the deep. With the right one removes the wicked, like bursting open a river. In this cast yin and yang, though not in their proper places, have one yang in the middle and three yang below — the image of the noble man ordering chaos and using the firm to decide against the yielding. Divining about governing and ruling the people, capturing fugitives, and punishing rebels is all auspicious. In a lawsuit one prevails by the right; one should not be secret or selfish. The noble man who obtains it has great fortune; the petty man the reverse.

name: Hexagram of the Not-Yet-Returned
note: A host of yin restraining yang; Kan, Water, due north
xiang: The fields lie waste and the soil is hollow; the people move their dwellings away. Await the year's abundance, and then return to the old cottage.
yan: In this hexagram yin rises to its extreme, and yang cannot restrain it. The fields lie waste and the people are scattered; only in a year of abundance do they return. The sick recover slowly. For the traveler it is unfavorable.
he: The scholar and official have no emolument; the traveler has not returned; fields and silkworms lose their profit. Though this hexagram is not auspicious, it cannot harm a person; only be content in poverty, keep to quiet, and do good deeds, and it will turn auspicious of itself.
chen: Two yin are above and four yin below; the one yang is solitary and weak, and the way of earth is void and damaged — the image of wandering and moving about for many years. Hence the saying.
liu: The fields lie waste and the soil is hollow — nothing can be relied upon. The petty man's desires are at odds, and in the end they will not share with one. Holding to the right and waiting, one is sure to obtain one's place. In this cast yang is sunk into yin, and below it leans upon the flourishing yin; hence the image of waste fields, hollow soil, and people fleeing and scattering. Yet the yin below is already old and does not seek union; the petty man, having attained his aim, at his extreme is sure to decline, while the lesser yin above, on the contrary, draws near to me. Therefore one in the end returns to the old cottage. Affairs divined are sure to have obstructions; keeping still and awaiting the season is auspicious.
shi:
Quarrels and slander bring turmoil;
enterprises are sure to be harmed.
If you seek the aid of secret virtue,
then you will be seen to escape calamity.

name: Hexagram of Caution and Vigilance
note: Two yang facing the center; Kun, Earth, southwest
xiang: Though safe, it is still perilous; though joyful, it is still mournful. Ever fearing separation, one cannot stay with another.
yan: Two yin dwell facing each other, with no yang position at all; their wills are not matched, and they are ever as if about to part. In this hexagram, what is done is unfavorable, and marriage is hard to join, because of the pure yin. In all affairs one must be cautious and vigilant.
he: There is about to be a separation, and good and evil are not discerned; what is sought is hard to gain. One should be careful in family affairs, for there is fear of secret plots. A campaign does not win, and official matters are not resolved. A hundred affairs are inauspicious.
chen: Both positions are weak yin, and their wills do not respond to each other; there is the image of parting. Hence the saying.
liu: Though safe, it is still perilous — the household is empty. Ever fearing separation — the wills are not alike. In this cast two yin dwell without, with no household; one thinks oneself safe and does not know the danger, and moreover the wills are not matched and there is nothing to rely upon. The diviner who obtains it finds what he does unfulfilled and the family fortune declining; there will be a sorrow that cannot be dispelled.

name: Hexagram of Guarding Against Greed
note: Two yin reversing position; Zhen, Thunder, due east
xiang: Burying gold and hiding jade, one boasts of one's own worth. The debts to ghosts are not discharged, and the spirits send down no blessing.
yan: With yang dwelling below and being trapped by yin, hence it is said 'burying gold and hiding jade.' And so, though one boasts of utmost worth, the spirits do not protect him. The sick have a ghostly influence and should pray at once. In official matters one is saved only by seeking the help of others.
he: In office, greed for wealth is sure to bring disaster and blame; though there are treasures, one is sure to worry about thieves. The sick have not recovered. The traveler has not returned. The imprisoned are hard to release. Fields and silkworms yield no harvest. A campaign is unfavorable, and one is seized by ghosts — speaking of its inauspiciousness. In this hexagram one should reform one's faults and cultivate virtue, and only then is one spared.
chen: Yang dwells in the position of earth — the resources of gold and jade; responding to the two, one covets them without end. Yet the position of Heaven is also yin and cannot bestow blessing; the way of Heaven diminishes the full, and ghosts and spirits harm the excessive. Hence the saying.
liu: Burying gold and hiding jade — yang is below. The way of ghosts sends its influence upward; blessing cannot be borrowed. In this cast lone yang is pressed beneath two yin and cannot act; while the two yin above are soft and irresolute, with nothing to stand upon. Hence there is no blessing and there is worry. The diviner should take greed as a warning.

name: Hexagram of Peace and Security
note: Pure yin unmoving; Kun, Earth, southwest
xiang: The year is rich and the months are prosperous; fields and lands are opened wide. Secure as Mount Tai, in the end there is no calamity.
yan: Open wide the fields and wait for the year to come full circle; using what Heaven allots and dividing the earth, in the end there is no calamity or fault. Its security is unmoving, like Mount Tai. Dwelling at home is auspicious. Fields and silkworms bring a great harvest. The sick have no suffering. The traveler has not returned.
he: In office one enjoys emolument, and wealth and silk come of themselves. An army gains its ground. The pregnant will bear a son, one of learning. This hexagram is greatly auspicious and profitable.
chen: All three positions are yin, yet not reaching the extreme of fullness. There is no image of one-sided triumph or mutual conflict, but the principle of receiving blessing in compliance and joy. Hence the saying. Opposite to one above, one in the middle, and one below, all are first yin and first yang; pure and harmonious with no conflict, and so all are auspicious.
liu: Years and months rich and prosperous — the minds of all are one. Gentle, compliant, and firm in integrity — blessing without end. Secure as Mount Tai — it has both beginning and end. In this cast all three positions are yin, attaining the central and correct; there is the image of dwelling at peace and resting in compliance, with no longing for what is outside. Hence there is fortune and no misfortune. Divining about the household, fields and silkworms, office, and trade — all affairs are greatly auspicious. In war one gains the ground. The sick recover without treatment, and public lawsuits hold no blame. The traveler has not returned.
shi:
A stretch of land in the central plain;
in deep spring, rain and dew abound.
Using Heaven and following the earth's advantage,
one rests in his calling and delights in peace and warmth.

name: Hexagram of Flourishing Fortune
note: Yin and yang wholly auspicious; Zhen, thunder of the due east.
xiang: Heaven-sent blessings he receives, rising as the sun ascends; office found in youthful years, rank and riches never end.
yan: Staying at home and seeking wealth is auspicious. The traveler has not yet returned; the sick should offer prayer and sacrifice. It is also said: abundant yang is stirring, like the sun in its ascent. This approaches pure good fortune. It is fitting to travel, but not fitting to dwell in seclusion or to hide away. In buying and selling and in dealings with servants, it is hard to get one’s wishes; all else is greatly auspicious.
he: Whatever one undertakes is lofty and far-reaching, and will surely fulfill one’s aim. The sick will come to no harm. A military expedition will win victory. In all affairs, one should not engage in what is secret or underhanded.
chen: With yin above and yang below, this is the image of heaven and earth in harmony, while the earthly path is rich in yang. The two yin lines above respond to the heavenly spirits and join with them, forming an image of blessings and emolument filled to overflowing. Hence the text says as above.
liu: Yang flourishes and rises from below; the firm prevails over the yielding. One advances in virtue and perfects one’s work, receiving Heaven’s blessing. In this hexagram two yin lines dwell above and abundant yang lies below, advancing upward like the rising sun. For seeking office and advancement in rank, divination is greatly auspicious. Yan Youming says: staying home and seeking wealth is auspicious; the traveler has not returned; the sick should pray and sacrifice. This hexagram is wholly auspicious; only dwelling in seclusion, fleeing, buying and selling, and dealing with servants are unfitting. He Chengtian says: whatever is undertaken is lofty and far-reaching and will surely fulfill one’s aim; in all affairs one should not engage in what is secret.
shi: When destiny meets the wind and cloud, he rests in the sun and moon’s bright glow; auspicious smoke drifts through the jeweled hall, the clear moon lights the golden couch below.

name: Hexagram of Smooth Success
note: Pure yin in its place; Kun, earth of the southwest.
xiang: Rich as a wellspring’s flow, drawn on yet never spent; every wish finds fulfillment, and gladness has no end.
yan: In the Book of Changes, Kun is thick and bears all things; its virtue joins with the boundless. The three positions are all yin, so nothing overcomes anything else and all affairs are auspicious. At home there will be happy, festive events. The traveler will soon return. Wealth is like a wellspring, inexhaustible in use. Whatever one seeks will be gained, with joy beyond compare. The sick will first be distressed, then recover.
he: In office one is highly promoted; one’s livelihood grows rich and ample; sericulture yields a doubled harvest — all is auspicious and joyful. The sick will recover of themselves. The imprisoned will be released. Marriage is favorable and harmonious. This hexagram is greatly auspicious.
chen: The three positions are all yin and abundant, holding the resources of accumulated wealth and honor; drawn upon without end, like a spring that flows through. Hence the text says as above.
liu: Wealth like a wellspring means gaining the advantage of the land. Yielding and obedient, it moves upward; there is no request that fails. In this hexagram the lower position holds abundant yin that does not oppose or contend with the upper, and so it is the image of rich, fertile soil. The two yin lines above are gentle and obedient, acting without rashness and resting content in their advantage; this is why the hexagram is auspicious. For the diviner, seeking any affair is greatly auspicious.
shi: Morning rain just cleared, the emerald stream shines bright; fold on fold of spring color mounts the rustic door. Gold that never fails has made the household rich — why should one pine for brocade robes and more?

name: Hexagram of Great Completion
image: Image of Knowing When to Stop
note: Upright yang at the center; Zhen, thunder of the due east.
xiang: Across my fields the carriage rolls, its wheels go rumbling on; and what are those treasures it brings? Gold of yellow, silver of white; keeping abundance ever full, never to fear want’s blight.
yan: The yang position dwells at the center, its will responding to what is without; there is great prosperity, blessing, and emolument, and no fear of poverty. This hexagram is auspicious. Plans and long views are realized, and there is cause for rejoicing.
he: Either through someone who comes one obtains goods, or by going to seek someone one gains wealth. All affairs are in harmony; the sick are at ease; those who have traveled far arrive; this is a greatly auspicious hexagram. Seeking office succeeds harmoniously; the traveler gains much and soon returns; litigation dissolves; and it is especially fitting to seek help.
chen: The human way is rich in yang, and the two yin lines respond to it — an image of wealth and sufficiency. Hence the text says as above.
liu: “Passing along my field-paths” means the firm and the yielding respond to each other. “His carriage rumbles on” means the position is upright and central. “Never to fear poverty” means there is great cause for celebration. In this hexagram all divinations are auspicious; but since it lacks the earthly position, managing property and establishing a career are unfavorable in one’s native place and favorable abroad. In general, hexagrams lacking the lower position are like this.
shi: Take Heaven’s emolument, and blessings will descend; keep full yet never spill, guard well, and all goes well; be neither slack nor proud, and keep your peace endowed.

name: Hexagram of Sorrow and Joy
note: Yin dwelling in the heavenly place; Dui, lake of the due west.
xiang: The mind is beset with care, sleepless, bright-eyed through the night; fearing that disaster comes, yet blessing arrives instead; with congratulations and delight, a great advantage to me.
yan: Though at first there is anxiety, in the end there is joy. It is also said: yin dwelling in the heavenly place is not its proper ground. Therefore, though there is anxiety, the three yang lines guard together, and it can do no harm. This hexagram first brings small anxiety, then great good fortune; hence there is no blame.
he: Disputes come to nothing; the traveler will arrive. In marriage and in trade, matters are difficult at first and easy afterward. The sick are first distressed, then recover. Official affairs begin in anxiety and end in good fortune. Lost things are hard to recover.
chen: The three yang lines dwell at the center, so the human way is by nature flourishing. Above are two yin lines, which respond to the single yang in the lower position. The central position is cut off from above and below, and so at first there is anxiety. Yet so abundant are the three yang that the two yin cannot come between them; in the end one will gain one’s aim. Hence the text says as above.
liu: With yin set over yang, the position is not fitting. To gain blessing amid anxiety and trouble comes from firmness at the center. In this hexagram yin dwells above and yang below — an image of not being in one’s proper place. Yet one yang lies below and abundant yang occupies the center, and the weak yin cannot restrain the firm; though at first there is doubt, in the end there is good fortune and celebration. In all such matters, anxiety at the start gives way to fortune at the end: the anxiety is empty, the fortune real.
shi: Who knew that success would rise like to heaven? In old age, many cares keep him awake at night; then suddenly he sees his old garden’s fine spring, where butterflies flit and vie in blossoms bright.

name: Hexagram of Peace and Safety
note: Yin above and below; Kan, water of the due north.
xiang: Above and below alike at peace, the heart breeds no deceit; serene and free of care, give no ear to wandering rumor.
yan: A heart that is upright is of itself auspicious; do not trust wandering rumor. The traveler will arrive; the prisoner will be released. Though above and below are both yin, three yang dwell at the center; at first there may seem to be anxiety and blame, but if each rests content in its own place, there will be no regret at all. All affairs go as they should; anxiety comes first, good fortune after. Serving one’s lord and forming friendships grow ever more excellent.
he: In marrying, one gains a beautiful wife; the traveler is on the road. A pregnant woman bears a son. The sick, and those who see strange apparitions, will come to no harm. Official affairs dissolve. Farming and sericulture yield harvest. A military expedition suffers loss; in trade and in all affairs there is good fortune.
chen: The human way is now flourishing, the two yin lines above and below respond to it, and the three yang also restrain themselves; hence the text says as above.
liu: Above and below are both yielding, for the center is their ruler. Firm, upright, and unbending, it wins the allegiance of all. In this hexagram three yang occupy the center while above and below are all yin; the lesser yin is not yet strong, so there is no discord or contention but only harmony and union. The yang is firm and abundant, and yin cannot overcome it; hence it is the image of peace above and below. There is good fortune and no misfortune. He Chengtian says: in this hexagram, divining about marriage brings a beautiful wife; the traveler is on the road; official affairs are dissolved; all affairs are auspicious.
shi: A pair of swallows return to the south, seeking the mansions of the Wangs and the Xies; the painted hall is still in the spring day, and here they commit their lives to rest.

name: Hexagram of Warding Off Evil
note: Yin weak, yang strong; Dui, lake of the due west.
xiang: All people hold me dear, driving away disaster and harm; the mad dog does not bite, and every affair bears fruit.
yan: In all affairs there is good fortune and one gains the help of others. The traveler returns and obtains goods and wealth; staying at home is likewise auspicious. It is also said: though yin dwells above, it is not in its rightful place. The host of yang grows ever more abundant and can drive away disaster and harm, so that all hold it dear. In this hexagram and the two before it, the upper position is held by usurpation; but the virtue of yang is undiminished, and if one cultivates it there will be good fortune. Whatever one worries about brings no suffering.
he: Dukes, lords, and regional governors will surely gain good counselors. In marrying, one will surely gain a good wife. The sick recover. The bound prisoner is released, having been rescued by someone. In battle there is victory. A pregnant woman bears a son. Trade brings profit.
chen: The human way is flourishing, and the earthly way is flourishing too. There is a dignity to be held in awe, driving away the wicked and the hidden. Although there are two yin lines above, they cannot bring harm.
liu: Modesty and light dwell above, and all hold it dear. A host of worthies give aid and support, guaranteeing that no harm will come. In this hexagram yin occupies the upper position but does not abuse its power. The host of yang below is firm, upright, and without crookedness; even a fierce dog will not bite, and will instead drive away disaster and harm on my behalf. Divining about affairs, one gains the help of many, and there will be success.
shi: A dragon spouts water in the heart of spring; the dew-drenched plants and trees all burst anew. Gladly an old man speaks to me in person: from this dead end my path now opens through.

name: Hexagram of Great Gain
note: Central yang restraining yin; Kan, water of the due north.
xiang: The Han hound pursues the hare, who cannot stretch a step; the biter of hares is before, the pursuer close behind; again and again the quarry is taken, and the hare cannot get away.
yan: The three yang at the center can restrain a host of petty men, just as a fierce hound seizes a hare that cannot get away — the capture comes before one can turn on one’s heel. In all affairs, what is small at first becomes great later. This hexagram is good for catching fugitives; seeking wealth is also abundant, and hunting brings many a catch. For the sick it is unfavorable.
he: Staying at home is auspicious. The traveler is delayed. The sick are distressed. The prisoner is held back. Official affairs are hard to resolve. A military expedition returns empty-handed.
chen: The human way is rich in yang and the earthly way rich in yin; yin and yang respond to each other, and both are abundant and accumulated; hence the text.
liu: The three yang at the center show the way of firmness flourishing. Petty men are subdued by gentleness and cannot contend. Though they would leap about, in the end they obey. In this hexagram the three yang stand between the two yin; the lesser yin is above and the mature yin below, the young and old at odds in desire, both held by firmness and unable to join together — hence the image of the Han hound pursuing the hare. The diviner who obtains this hexagram should greatly favor catching fugitives and chastising bandits; seeking wealth, seeking profit, and seeking marriage are all auspicious. Going out is obstructed. The bound prisoner is hard to release. The sick are in grave danger. Staying at home is without blame. In all divinations, seeking a thing succeeds, while undoing a thing does not.
shi: The world’s path is free of briar and thorn; O heart, do not in self-reproach abide; pursue your name, pursue your gain as well, and through hard toil your livelihood provide.

name: Hexagram of Succoring the Perilous
note: Upright yin at the center; Kun, earth of the southwest.
xiang: The sage, refined and elegant — what manner of form is his? The worthy and good answer from within: first weeping, then singing. It is also said: yesterday I went out on a journey, and met with disaster head-on; a stray arrow struck me, and my eyes streamed with tears.
yan: What sets the sage apart from ordinary men is that his substance is refined and balanced, and only thereby does he become worthy of honor. This hexagram first brings anxiety, then joy. If one wishes to see a ruler or to seek office and emolument, there is no proper beginning, but there will be an end.
he: Where one goes is not auspicious; one may meet armed bandits and be shot in the eye. The traveler does not come. The sick are in the utmost distress. Official affairs are hard to dissolve. With gossip and wrangling on every side, only by seeking blessings will one find peace. It is not fitting to travel by boat. Keeping to the old ways brings good fortune.
chen: The yin above is weak, the lower position falls empty, and a host of yin dwell at the center; there is no ground on which to stand — an image of peril and disorder. “Succor the perilous, keep integrity” is meant as admonition and warning, yet no such person appears. The divination text speaks of a sage, refined and worthy and good, who keeps integrity — this does not match the hexagram image. I suspect another edition: “Yesterday I went out and met with disaster; a stray arrow struck my eye, my tears streaming” — a hexagram of misfortune with no good fortune. This wording is probably the correct one.
liu: “Going out and meeting disaster” means yin has seized the center. “A stray arrow strikes the eye” means the upper position is exhausted. In this hexagram the upper and middle are both yin; there is no lower position and no proper pair, so the lines injure one another. The diviner who obtains it will be oppressed and wronged by petty men of the yin sort. The traveler must fear robbers; official affairs are hard to resolve; using troops brings wounds and defeat; marriage is discordant; in all things there is blame.
shi: Clouds lie across the mountain ridge, the waters stretch wide and dim; a thousand miles of road, and I gaze toward my native home. Since hardship comes of its own accord, do not grieve, good sir — leaning at the gate in sorrow, I stand in the slanting sun.

name: Hexagram of Decline Revived
note: Weak yang rising below; Zhen, thunder of the due east.
xiang: Sages and worthies succeed one another; what was faint revives again; like gourd-vines trailing on and on, step by step it climbs upward.
yan: Affairs, though first gone awry, are restored again; whatever is sought will surely be gained, and all affairs follow the heart. It is also said: though the yang is faint and weak, its will is set on the upright; rising from below toward the heights, like the tendrils of the gourd that trail ever upward, if one works at affairs with an upright heart, one will revive the faint and continue what was cut off. This hexagram governs promotion in office; praying for favor, seeking blessings, and desiring heirs are all auspicious.
he: Those pursuing learning will succeed. The traveler will soon arrive. Farming and sericulture bring a harvest; trade brings profit. In marrying, one gains a chaste and beautiful wife. In office one rises and advances, and all one seeks follows the heart. The sick fall into a deep sleep; seeking the gods brings good fortune. Lost things are not recovered.
chen: Four yin at the center form the image of decline and weakness; but one yang below means the root of goodness still survives. Two yin above respond to that one yang — the image of Heaven protecting the good. Hence the text says as above.
liu: When yin flourishes at the center, at its extreme it must decline. “The gourd-vines trail on” means yang’s summer is coming. “Step by step it rises” means the upright way returns. In this hexagram the lesser yang lies beneath a host of yin, and is perilously alone indeed. Yet the lesser yin above and the mature yin at the center are not of one mind; petty men at the height of their power must fall out among themselves, while the lesser yang is just now rising below. As the one declines by the day, the other advances by the day, like gourd-vines trailing upward — the sign of reviving what has declined and setting right what is disordered. Divination about affairs is auspicious.
shi: In dream I enter the road to Tiantai; I climb the mountain, and the moon shines clear. How strange — the spring scene is changed, and I see once more the old flowers in full bloom.

name: Hexagram of Averting Disaster
note: Yang scattered, yin at its extreme; Kun, earth of the southwest.
xiang: Summer goes, autumn comes, bitter frost brings harm; birds and beasts moult their coats, plants and trees shed leaves and roots.
yan: In all affairs, spring is the beginning and things follow the heart; staying at home is auspicious; the traveler has not returned. It is also said: going out in summer and hiding in autumn, yang is scattered and yin at its extreme; therefore birds and beasts moult, and grass and trees lose their color. This is the gentleman’s time of the darkening of the light — a time to dwell in stillness, and not to press forward in worldly affairs. This hexagram is mildly inauspicious.
he: Those in office meet with reckless villains, and vicious men do them harm. The sick are in danger and distress. A military expedition is unfavorable. Official affairs are hard to resolve. The traveler has not yet come. One’s livelihood is displaced, and there may be disputes, robbers, and fighting.
chen: It is a time when yin flourishes and the human way is weak and declining; one should not act or move, for disaster and upheaval are about to arise.
liu: “Summer goes and autumn comes” means the yin vital force is flourishing. “Grass and trees shed leaves and roots” means one keeps still and guards the upright. In this hexagram a host of yin hold sway and mature yin sits at the center — a time when the gentleman’s way is blocked. The diviner should withdraw, hide away, and keep stillness, and should not seek to advance; in all divinations, one will not obtain what one seeks. The sick are in great distress.
shi: Rash walking meets the earth’s net; a hasty move enters heaven’s snare. Only prudence is the higher course — withdraw your person and keep your peace.

name: Hexagram of Dispelling Ignorance
note: Yin transformed, yang arrives; Zhen, thunder of the due east.
xiang: Yin at its extreme, yang is born; hibernating creatures stir and open; a great amnesty is proclaimed through the land, with bells and drums resounding.
yan: When yin turns into yang, it startles the host of hibernating creatures, as if beating bells and drums; there are great prisons to be opened. This is the hexagram of receiving a mandate and founding institutions. For advancement in office it is greatly auspicious. It is not fitting for marriage, because yin and yang injure each other and are not in harmony.
he: Great mercy reaches down, and all things are richly moistened. The bound are released. Those in office rise high. In the use of affairs all things succeed, and one’s livelihood increases tenfold.
chen: This classic also makes the hexagrams before and after explain one another. In the preceding hexagram yin was at its extreme; here two changes to three, and yang occupies the earthly position — the image of order restored after utter disorder. Hence the text says as above.
liu: “Yin at its extreme turns to yang” means the firm has come within. “Hibernating creatures open” means thunder bursts from the earth. “Bells and drums resound” means the sound of virtue spreads abroad. In this hexagram the three yang decide against yin at its fullest, like the thunder that rouses hibernating creatures. It is a time when the gentleman’s way is growing; all divinations are auspicious. In using troops, one should spread civil virtue.
shi: Yin at its end now meets the time of peace; the sleeping worm’s door opens to the light. With three strong yang, act now and take the field — both fame and gain will come to you outright.

name: Hexagram of Sickness and Sorrow
note: Yin at its extreme becomes excess; Kun, earth of the southwest.
xiang: Yin in excess, a minor ailment; fallen flat, the heart is full of sorrow; he turns his face upward to heaven, then prostrates himself, bowing low.
yan: What one seeks is not gained, and the traveler meets with trouble. It is also said: when yin becomes illness, it arises by gradual insinuation; since it has not reached the extreme, it is called a minor ailment. Yet the fallen man gazes up to heaven and sees no rescuer, and so he bows low and prostrates himself, given over to anxious brooding. In this hexagram all affairs are inauspicious; only caution and secrecy are fitting.
he: The sick cannot be saved. The imprisoned find their guilt confirmed. The traveler is at the end of his resources. This hexagram is inauspicious.
chen: The human way is weak in yin and the earthly way is yin at its extreme — the image of illness and poverty. Above, even the heavenly spirits cannot save one; hence the text says as above.
liu: “Yin flourishes and spreads insidiously” means sorrow encounters calamity. “Prostrating oneself and gazing to heaven” means anxiety has reached its extreme. In this hexagram two yin are exhausted below and one yin perches above — this is an omen of misfortune. Divining about illness, death is certain. The imprisoned do not come out; those besieged find no rescue; in all things there is misfortune.
shi: Alas, my lot is harsh and the times run contrary; disaster strikes, and my body grows faint. High Heaven now looks not upon me; woe is me — this illness is perilous.

name: Hexagram of Restlessness
note: Three yang standing alone; Qian, heaven of the northwest.
xiang: Heaven and earth take their fixed forms, and from them humanity is born and transformed; drifting with the vital force, now up, now down, it cannot find rest in itself.
yan: Ruler and minister are jumbled together, with no settled place; each may go or stay as it pleases, with none restraining another. Though this hexagram carries no blame, all affairs are hard to bring into harmony.
he: In all affairs there is sure to be hardship and distress, and one cannot follow one’s heart. Official affairs are beset with doubt; the sick recover slowly.
chen: The three yang are by nature the beginning of the human way, yet they occupy the heavenly position — they have the image but not the place. Hence the text says as above.
liu: “Heaven and earth take form” means the beginning of all living things. “Drifting with the vital force, now up, now down” means nothing has yet found a settled dwelling. This hexagram shows a slight inclination in some direction, but it is not yet strong and flourishing.
shi: Fright and false alarms, and losses, and disasters come again; keep your going and your staying close, beware what lurks in the dark. If you can slip the tiger’s tail and the serpent’s head, then to keep this body safe you must still forfeit wealth.

name: Hexagram of Fruitless Labor
note: A lone yang without aid; Qian, heaven of the northwest.
xiang: Going east to gather herbs, he climbs Mount Tai; he finds no magic fungus, but only fragrant orchids; these are of no use at all, and he returns empty-handed.
yan: Within and without are pure yang, with nothing to respond to each other; doubled firmness above forms the image of a mountain. The central position is incomplete, so it is hard to accomplish merit; gathering herbs and finding orchids is the image of empty beauty. In all affairs there is a name but no substance: hearing good news, one is not glad; hearing bad news, one is not grieved.
he: A military expedition is inauspicious. What one seeks is not obtained. The orchid is no tool for use; he returns empty-handed, and in all affairs nothing is accomplished.
chen: Three yang above are at their height and yet useless. One yang below is solitary, weak, and unanswered. The central position is again vacant — what, after all, can be done!
liu: “Gathering herbs and finding orchids” means beauty without substance; “returning empty-handed” means there is no gain whatever. In this hexagram three yang above form the image of a mountain. Within and without are both yang, and the central position has nothing to answer it; hence there is empty beauty and no result. Achievements are hard to establish, and one should not attempt anything. Yan says: in this hexagram, hearing bad news one is not grieved, and hearing good news one is not glad.
shi: They speak of Luoyang’s flowers so fair, whose praise is on every tongue; he set out with high hopes one fine night, and returned to a home undone.

name: Hexagram of Flood Disaster
note: Yin and yang pressing on each other; Gen, mountain of the northeast.
xiang: Ceaseless falls the drenching rain; the floodwaters surge to the sky; the people dwell in nests in the trees, and no cooking fire sends up its smoke.
yan: Though within and without are upright, the central position is empty; yin and yang press upon each other, and so rain results. This hexagram carries much blame; dwelling at home is especially inauspicious, and farming and sericulture bring little harvest.
he: An omen of misfortune and disorder; nothing is fitting. Family members are at odds. Petty men of the yin sort are unfavorable; seeking wealth is hard to accomplish. The traveler has not returned. Disputes are not yet resolved. A military expedition suffers defeat. It is greatly fitting to keep to the old ways.
chen: Yang is at its extreme while yin holds sway, and the human position in the middle is vacant. The yin force is gradually flourishing; hence the text says as above.
liu: “The rainwaters surge to the sky” means growth from below. “Nests in the trees and no smoke” means excess above. In this hexagram three yang are in excess above and the lesser yin grows below, while the center has no master; hence, following its inclination, it descends as rain. Yang perches above and has nothing to make a home of — the image of dwelling in nests with no fire. For the diviner, this is inauspicious.
shi: Thorns grow on every side; the luan and phoenix find no perch. The mind is spent, the heart grows clumsy — how can it feast on grain and millet rich?

name: Hexagram of Drought Disaster
note: Rampant yang lacking yin; Qian, heaven of the northwest.
xiang: The blazing heat works harm; heaven and earth are parched. They ascend to heaven to beseech the dragon, and dig into the earth to seek a spring; in dread and fear, no one finds peace.
yan: Heaven and earth are both yang — the image of excess at its extreme. Beseeching the dragon and seeking a spring, nothing at all responds. This hexagram is greatly inauspicious. Farming and sericulture bring no profit; yet going far away, a thousand li from home, may be auspicious.
he: Drought and scorching heat bring disaster, for above there is no gracious moisture, and below the people are bound in ranks of resentment. Nothing succeeds; marriage, building, and seeking wealth are all unfavorable.
chen: Above and below are both rampant yang, with no yin to answer them; the central position is again empty — the image of drought. Hence the text says as above.
liu: “Heaven and earth are both yang” means the fire of drought blazes. “In dread and fear, no peace” means the position has been lost. In this hexagram above and below are both yang, and the human position is absent; yang alone cannot give birth, and so there is drought and disaster. In divination, nothing at all is accomplished.
shi: To press ahead is hard, and hard to draw back again; now a glad face, now a face of pain. As vain as fishing the moon from the eastern sea — all your striving ends in vanity.

name: Hexagram of the Distant Raid
note: Yin and yang in separate places; Gen, mountain of the northeast.
xiang: Pursuing the fleeing bandits, one goes as far as Lelang; recover my precious jade, and lead back my cattle and sheep.
yan: Heaven and earth respond to each other, and yin and yang have their places. Therefore one goes far, to the edge of the sea, and makes one’s campaign plain. But the central position has no master, and the precious jade, the cattle and sheep, cannot avoid being taken by the robbers. This hexagram is mildly auspicious. In all punitive expeditions there will be success. Lelang lies east of the sea.
he: If one takes another’s goods, it leads to misfortune; hasten to undo it and make amends, and there will be good fortune. Or if one takes things from within the household that ought not to be taken, that too is inauspicious. The traveler returns only after losing wealth; in all affairs, it is auspicious to part with money.
chen: Below is a host of yin — the image of thieves and robbers. The three yang are now flourishing and can command a general to pursue and chastise them, breaking their yin faction; hence the text says as above.
liu: “Pursuing the fleeing bandits” means going out to accomplish a punitive campaign. “Going as far as Lelang” means the toil of a distant expedition. “Leading back my cattle and sheep” means recovering one’s goods. In this hexagram yin and yang have their places and respond to each other, yet there is no central position; hence it is the image of being robbed and suffering loss. One must labor at a distant campaign and only then recover what was lost. The diviner will succeed only after toil, and in using troops there will be hardship first and victory after.
shi: A beast with two tails — the affair is hard to complete; guard your fame and gain, lest both fall short and fail. Meet with a man of wood, and only then take heart; or if you meet with water, it too will serve your turn.

name: Hexagram of Flowing Blessings
note: Three yang above; Qian, heaven of the northwest.
xiang: Through long adversity unrelieved, now one meets with peace at last; not for a single season only — its shelter reaches down the generations.
yan: Three yang above, and nothing can encroach upon them; the ruler is enlightened, the ministers good, petty men withdraw from office, and so blessings and celebration can be brought about. In this hexagram, even if there is anxiety at first, afterward there is no suffering. Staying at home is auspicious; affairs begin to follow the heart. Emolument and rank are just now obtained. The traveler returns; the sick recover; what is sought is greatly auspicious.
he: Affairs begin with anxiety, and afterward blessings arrive. It is favorable to meet a great man; goods and wealth are gained twofold; official affairs are resolved. A military expedition is swift and victorious. Seals, credentials, and documents arrive; only marriage is unfavorable.
chen: The human way is upright, and the way of Heaven is bright and luminous, shining down upon those below, who receive Heaven’s blessings; hence the text says as above.
liu: “Through long adversity” means there is anxiety at first. “Now meeting with peace” means one finally obtains what one sought. In this hexagram the upper and middle are yang with nothing to oppose or obstruct them. Minds and ways are in accord, so blessings and celebration can be brought about — the image of gaining Heaven. In all affairs there is regret first and joy after.
shi: The storm has now fallen still; your boat meets waters calm and clear. Henceforth your fame and deeds are done — why sigh that white has come to your hair?

name: Hexagram of Radiant Yang
note: The yang host in power; Qian, heaven of the northwest.
xiang: Take office in good season; your emolument matches your years. Labor earnestly at your affairs, and be careful not to let it slip.
yan: Taking office in good season, both going out and staying are fitting; blessing and emolument come in their turn; one should be prudent and careful, and must not grow slack. The sick recover slowly. Though the traveler returns, there are obstructions on the road. It is also said: cast off the accumulated yin and drive the host of yang; a doubled brightness shines in splendor, and one beholds the glory of the realm. As for position, all affairs are at peace. Other external matters may also be advanced by seizing the season. Marriage and seeking office are all the more auspicious.
he: Whatever is sought should be undertaken at a favorable time. The sick should pray for blessings. The traveler may arrive. The imprisoned, by petitioning the magistrate, may be spared.
chen: Abundant yang above shines down upon the earth below; the human way and the earthly way are each a single yang, advancing and never retreating, favorable for getting through.
liu: “Yang bright in its proper place” means the way greatly prospers. “The gentleman’s service” means acting in good season. In this hexagram three yang occupy the proper position, while the middle and lower are lesser yang just now rising; the way of yang is smooth and open, and the crookedness of yin is thrust aside. Office-holding and the practice of the way should be seized at this time; in divination, one should greatly favor advancing, and must not miss the hour. All affairs are auspicious. Only what is secret and underhanded is unfitting.
shi: The east wind stirs, and the nine-fold gates swing open; a gentle air comes down from the sun on high. From this day on, in all things there is joy — ride the clouds, and in one leap ascend the Jasper Terrace.

name: Hexagram of Heaven’s Protection
note: Yin and yang in mutual accord; Xun, wind of the southeast.
xiang: Climbing high and gazing far, he sees the highway of Heaven; the Jade Maiden and Confucius the Sage hand him a sacred talisman; granting eternal agelessness, to keep his body safe.
yan: The image of gaining help. Affairs come through a woman; staying at home is auspicious; office and rank rise with honor; study is brought to great completion. The traveler has not returned, but will surely gain rare and wonderful things. The sick recover of themselves. It is also said: the earthly position is upright, and Heaven and humanity unite in virtue — like climbing high and surveying the six directions, while below one responds to yin. One gains one’s proper mate; the divine talisman is given to me; one may look up and see it, and reach a hundred years of age while sitting still. This is the hexagram of the honored: yin and yang gain their places, neither overcomes nor injures the other, and all affairs are greatly auspicious.
he: Holding office is auspicious; in marrying one gains a beautiful wife. The traveler’s road is open. The sick linger. Official affairs, petitioning a great minister, farming and sericulture, and trade are all auspicious. A pregnant woman bears a son.
chen: The human way and the earthly way, with yin and yang responding to each other, and three yang in Heaven shining down upon the earth below; hence the text says as above.
liu: “Climbing high and gazing far” means dwelling in the upper place. “The Jade Maiden gives the talisman” means yin comes to join it. Central, upright, and answered, one gains Heaven’s protection. In this hexagram one yang is at the center, receiving above the summons of firm brightness and answering below to the mate of lesser yin; its good fortune is beyond compare.
shi: Though a jewel on the mat be precious, it must still wait for a buyer’s price; when your luck comes, all is smooth and fair — in every affair, no scheming will suffice.

name: Hexagram of Honor and Nobility
note: Yang bright above and below; Qian, heaven of the northwest.
xiang: His bright virtue shines with great light, endless life, boundless long; the seven stars of the Northern Dipper stand guard and watch for me; he gains promotion in rank and pay, prosperous and blessed through the generations.
yan: What is sought is gained; the traveler returns. It is also said: above and below are both yang, within and without illuminating one another — this is not a thing for common folk; it is the hexagram of honor and nobility. If one wishes to see a ruler, it is like attending him facing north.
he: In office one is promoted in rank; study is brought to completion. An expedition gains its ground, and the army suffers no harm. The sick should pray to the heavenly spirits. Marriage is fitting. Trade brings profit. The traveler will soon return. Sericulture and grain are harvested. Official affairs dissolve. This hexagram is greatly auspicious.
chen: The human way is upright, the earthly way is rich in yang, and three yang above look down from on high — the image of wealth, honor, and long life. Hence it is called honorable and noble, and favorable for seeing the eminent.
liu: “Bright virtue shines with great light” means the way of yang is radiant. “The Dipper stands guard” means hidden yin is dissolved. In this hexagram, seeking office and planning affairs, one gains the strength of a noble man. Planning a tomb or dwelling, one will surely obtain an auspicious site. Those who stay have help; those who travel have company. This is the hexagram of the noble; even a common person who obtains it will have extraordinary joy.
shi: No danger lies before your cart; your boat drifts to a ford with ease. The rain and dew fall from the sky, and gate and courtyard are renewed.

name: Hexagram of Fitting Prayer
note: Accumulated yin overcoming yang; Xun, wind of the southeast.
xiang: Time and again strange sights appear; one must summon the shaman and the seer; pray and seek blessing, that disaster may melt and calamity cease; great and small alike find peace, by the power of the spirits.
yan: It surely presages seeing strange things. In all affairs, at first one’s wishes are not met, but afterward all follow the heart. The traveler will return, but there will first be a letter. Staying at home is auspicious. It is also said: with accumulated yin intruding upon the extreme yang, it is like sitting upright and beholding strange sights. The shamans and seers spoken of answer to the upper position, and so prayer is fitting. To be able to disperse disaster and trouble — is this not the power of the spirits? In all affairs there is minor good fortune.
he: There is fear of disaster and calamity, and one should cultivate blessings to avert them. There may be disputes and quarrels, lawsuits and troubles, or evil dreams and strange sights; misfortune comes first and fortune after, difficulty at the start and ease at the end — good and ill in equal measure. It is fitting to be vigilant, to keep still, and to cultivate religious rites. For the sick, appealing to the heavenly spirits is auspicious. Marriage comes together suddenly, because within and without there is response.
chen: One yang at the center means the human way is solitary and weak; three above in Heaven and four below on earth shine and answer one another — the image of spirits manifesting themselves.
liu: “Time and again strange sights appear” means the heart is beset with doubt. There is an old ghost in the house, and one’s strength cannot govern it. Report it to the bright spirits, and one is assured of no harm. Here deep-accumulated yin lies within, while the upper position holds abundant yang; hence the central position is darkened. The diviner who obtains this will have strange sights in his home and should suppress them. For illness and litigation too, prayer and entreaty are fitting; in all affairs, anxiety comes first and good fortune after.
shi: Sorrow comes to the point of pain; anxiety arrives — be on your guard within. Only when you have passed through cold and heat can you escape from disaster and harm.

name: Hexagram of Late Fulfillment
note: Yang arrayed above yin; Gen, mountain of the northeast.
xiang: Shouldering the plow, he tills the field himself; in the fourth month he lifts his foot to go; earnestly he seizes the season, and the grain grows lush and thick.
yan: Three yang dwell above, and the yin lines stand properly in the center; the positions accord with their principle. Sowing at the right season brings abundant profit. The fourth month is full yang, when grain and millet begin to flourish; farming and sericulture are auspicious.
he: All affairs are auspicious, only a little slow. Whether staying home or going far away, seeking wealth is greatly auspicious. A military expedition is victorious; the traveler arrives. The hexagram image has no contention; after the fourth month it is fitting to set affairs in motion.
chen: The human way is weak in yin and cannot accomplish things quickly; yet three yang above receive Heaven’s blessing, and one may have one’s wishes; hence the text says as above.
liu: With yin following yang, the position is right and proper. Tilling in good season means one fulfills one’s hopes. In this hexagram the three yang gain their positions and yin follows them — the image of obedience without resistance. But since there is no earthly position, one must work diligently and in good season, and only then can there be gain.
shi: A road lies ahead; do not chafe at delay; how long to sift gold from the sand? Wash away all the grit and the gold will show — twofold fame and twofold gain, both to hand.

name: Hexagram of Delivered Goods
note: Yin gaining the outer yang; Li, fire of the due south.
xiang: A guest comes from the south, bringing me fine materials; precious goods and rare curios, bowls of gold and cups of jade.
yan: It presages someone sending gifts that arrive; staying at home is auspicious, the traveler returns, and one gains treasures and goods and wealth. It is also said: with yin at the center responding to the yang without, a friend comes from afar — is this not fitting? The south is the place of yang, hence “comes from the south.” Precious goods and rare curios are the wherewithal of the noble; bowls of gold and cups of jade are the furnishings of a fine banquet.
he: Marriage is auspicious. What is sought is gained. The sick recover. Trade brings profit. Official affairs dissolve. The traveler arrives. This hexagram is greatly auspicious.
chen: One and two respond to each other, and one yang occupies the earthly position — the image of wealth. Three yang above shine their bright light downward.
liu: “A guest comes from the south” means the firm responds. “Bowls of gold and cups of jade” serve to show respect. In this hexagram lesser yin is at the center, one yang is its neighbor below, and abundant yang gains its place above; yin, gentle and obedient, responds to the yang without, and so one is sure to gain precious goods arriving from the south. “Coming from the south” means the upper three are Li; Li is the southern region. “Bowls of gold and cups of jade” means the lower one is Qian; Qian is metal and jade, the image of golden bowls and jade cups. The upper’s respondent, paired with the center, is the receiver of the guest’s gift. For the diviner, seeking wealth and forming marriages, all affairs are greatly auspicious.
shi: In the Golden Valley the flowers bloom in profusion; a host of immortals gather, dim and distant, on the Jasper Terrace. Pouring gold and jade, they startle the diviner’s eye, drinking the spring wind together, how many times a day!

name: Hexagram of No Hardship
note: Yin not encroaching on yang; Gen, mountain of the northeast.
xiang: The land is peaceful and safe, with no hardship or difficulty; greatly fitting for planting and toil, favorable for going out and coming back.
yan: The lower position does not encroach upon the upper, and so it is said the land is peaceful and safe; sowing is fitting, trade brings profit, and in office one rises and advances. Divining about illness there is no blame; the traveler is safe and will arrive sooner or later; marriage is harmonious; the dwelling is auspicious.
he: The seeker’s wishes are fulfilled. The sick recover lightly. Official affairs bring no worry. Greatly auspicious.
chen: The middle and lower are both yin, not yet reaching the extreme; the earthly way is pure and fine, and three yang shine down upon it; yin and yang are harmonious and free-flowing — the image of a bountiful harvest.
liu: “The land is peaceful and safe” means the yielding dwells in the low place. “No hardship” means the heart is free of doubt. With no deceit above or below, what is there that is not fitting? In this hexagram firm yang is above, and the middle and lower are in harmonious obedience; hence the land is peaceful and without hardship, and whether one moves or stays, advances or retreats, there is nothing to be hidden or feared. In divination, nothing is inauspicious.
shi: The sea is broad, the clouds part, the post-road stretches far; a bright phoenix bears an edict down to the world’s edge. The people rejoice in their work, secure as a wall, and one’s merit and fame are praised by all the age.

name: Hexagram of Deference and Harmony
note: Yin and yang in obedient accord; Li, fire of the due south.
xiang: The one above is square and upright; those below perform their duties; the household is harmonious, great and small join their strength; whatever one wills meets no resistance, and all that is sought is gained.
yan: Yin occupies the central position — the image of carrying out and obeying; hence “those below perform their duties.” This hexagram unites and gains the strength of all those below. Everything sought is fulfilled.
he: Marriage is auspicious; husband and wife are in harmony. The dwelling is peaceful and safe. The traveler will soon arrive. Business, farming, and sericulture bring profit; a pregnant woman bears a son. Official affairs bring no suffering. A military expedition is greatly favorable.
chen: The human way is gentle and obedient; above and below are three yang; the household is substantial and full, and the family’s way is now flourishing — hence the text says as above.
liu: “Yang firm above” means square and upright. “The strong and the obedient carry on together” means those below perform their duties. The household is harmonious, and nothing sought fails to be gained. In this hexagram, holding office, dwelling at home, marching with troops, managing a livelihood, marriage, and trade — in all of these there is nothing unfavorable; everything sought is gained; it is a greatly auspicious hexagram.
shi: Joyous air fills gate and court; the household holds no grief or grudge. Where the noble one casts a kindly glance, from there the ford opens wide.

name: Hexagram of Contrariety and Conflict
note: Yin and yang in contrariety; Gen, mountain of the northeast.
xiang: The lower does not follow the upper; the center does not govern what is without; above and below oppose and overcome, and all order and discipline fall into ruin.
yan: The way of yin gradually grows, and yang cannot restrain it; thereby all goes astray and transgresses; hence it is called ruin and disorder. In this hexagram all affairs are inauspicious.
he: What is sought is not gained. What is undertaken does not succeed; treatment of illness is without effect. A military expedition meets defeat. The traveler has not returned; official affairs entangle one another; the imprisoned find it hard to come out, as if entering the gate of death. In all matters it is inauspicious, and it is not fitting to change anything. If divined in the first month, it is auspicious; in all others it is inauspicious.
chen: The human way is weak and soft and cannot govern the firm. Below is a host of petty men; above are three yang, yet the middle and lower are rich in yin; hence the text says as above.
liu: “The lower does not follow the upper” means yin flourishes and has its way. “Above and below oppose and overcome” means they prey upon one another. “Order and discipline fall into ruin” means in the end nothing can prevail. In this hexagram above and below overcome each other, and the yielding at the center can neither govern the host of petty men nor serve the upper in uprightness; its course must lead to ruin and disorder. For the diviner, all affairs are inauspicious.
shi: Meeting a mountain, you must shun the danger; meeting water, keep worry in your breast. On the day you return to your native village, know well the beast with two tails.

name: Hexagram of Serving the Sovereign
note: Two yang engendering each other; Qian, heaven of the northwest.
xiang: A wise sovereign rules above; below there is no hidden treachery. In court robes they stand in ordered ranks — no need for removing or advancing.
yan: Above is a wise sovereign and below are worthy ministers, and so there is no treachery; all stand in ordered ranks with due sequence. This hexagram is greatly auspicious and fitting for the joy of gaining position and emolument.
he: Anxiety first, joy after; taking office, all goes all the more well. The imprisoned are released. All affairs are auspicious. Seals, credentials, and documents arrive. In official affairs one gains the strength of a noble man; farming, sericulture, and livestock bring doubled profit. A military expedition is a great victory. Marriage is unfavorable.
chen: Heaven and humanity are pure yang — the image of a wise sovereign and good ministers; hence the text says as above.
liu: “A wise sovereign and good ministers” means no treachery. “In court robes in ordered ranks” means one should not change things overmuch. In this hexagram doubled yang occupies the positions of sovereign and minister, with no petty yin to come between them — it attains the highest good. All affairs are auspicious; it is fitting to keep to the old and not fitting to change. Only in divining about marriage, and about rain and moisture, does it fall short of one’s wishes.
shi: His horns now lower, now rear, half emerging from the cloud; his claws and fangs now formed, he is spared all toil. From this day, following the thunder’s transforming power, he is destined to be a man above the world of men.

name: Hexagram of Steadfast Longevity
note: Pure yang, three in accord; Qian, heaven of the northwest.
xiang: The Four White-haired Elders of Mount Shang, nourishing their nature, walking the Way, breathing in the primal vital force, attain agelessness.
yan: Though this hexagram is pure yang, it takes the lower position as its lord, approaching the image of the noble retreat; one may nourish one’s purity therein. In all affairs, peace and steadfastness bring good fortune; only marriage is unfavorable, because of the pure yang.
he: In office one is highly promoted. Farming and sericulture should be done early. The traveler arrives. Official affairs are resolved. The sick recover. In trade and in staying at home, all affairs are greatly auspicious.
chen: Three dwells in the upper and middle positions, the two responding to each other, while one yang below cannot advance upward — the image of a worthy man in a low place. With nothing to undertake, he dwells in seclusion and nourishes his long life; hence the text says as above.
liu: “The Four White-haired Elders of Mount Shang” means dwelling in seclusion while holding to brightness. “Breathing the primal force” means one may roam at ease.
